Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 6:44 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 4 Ohio State travels to No. 5 Indiana for a massive Big Noon showdown. Can the Buckeyes avenge last year's Big Ten Championship loss? One of the biggest games of the college football season is set for Saturday afternoon as No. 4 Ohio State travels to Bloomington to take on No. 5 Indiana in FOX's Big Noon Saturday showdown. And there is plenty of bad blood between these two programs. The last time these teams met, Indiana stunned Ohio State 13-10 in the 2025 Big Ten Championship Game, ending the Buckeyes' undefeated season. Now, Ryan Day and Ohio State have an opportunity to return the favor against Curt Cignetti's defending national champions. Ohio State enters at 5-1, while Indiana remains undefeated at 6-0. Both teams are 3-0 in Big Ten play, making this matchup potentially decisive in the conference championship race. Ohio State: Can Julian Sayin Deliver? Ohio State's offense has been explosive this season, averaging more than 42 points per game. Quarterback Julian Sayin has thrown for approximately 1,772 yards, while superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has been nearly unstoppable, recording 48 receptions for 916 yards and 11 touchdowns. Smith is the most dangerous player in college football, and Indiana's secondary will have its hands full trying to contain him. However, last year's championship game exposed some serious problems for Ohio State. Sayin threw for 258 yards, and Smith recorded eight catches for 144 yards, but the Buckeyes managed just 10 points. Sayin was also sacked five times. Indiana's defensive front remains dangerous, averaging 3.3 sacks and 8.2 tackles for loss per game this season. Running back Bo Jackson, who has rushed for approximately 460 yards, must help establish balance and prevent Indiana from focusing entirely on Sayin. Indiana: The Hoosiers Aren't Going Anywhere Indiana might have lost Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza, but Curt Cignetti has kept the Hoosiers rolling. TCU transfer Josh Hoover has thrown for more than 1,300 yards with 17 touchdowns and zero interceptions, while running back Turbo Richard has rushed for nearly 600 yards. Wide receiver Charlie Becker has also been outstanding, recording 529 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. Michigan State transfer Nick Marsh gives Indiana another dangerous weapon on the outside. Defensively, Indiana is allowing approximately 12 points per game and has demonstrated an ability to create pressure without sacrificing coverage. However, the Hoosiers haven't exactly dominated their recent competition. Indiana narrowly escaped Northwestern 29-23 before defeating Nebraska 20-17 last weekend. Those performances raise questions about whether the Hoosiers can consistently move the football against an elite opponent. Expect another physical, defensive battle between two legitimate College Football Playoff contenders. Indiana's defense will create problems for Sayin, and the Hoosiers should find success moving the football through Hoover and Richard. However, Ohio State has something Indiana doesn't: Jeremiah Smith. I expect Smith to deliver a massive performance, surpassing 100 receiving yards and making the difference in a game that comes down to the final possession. Sayin will make a few mistakes under pressure, but the Buckeyes' defense will get enough stops to escape Bloomington with a huge victory. Final Score: No. 4 Ohio State 24, No. 5 Indiana 20 Ohio State gets its revenge, hands Indiana its first loss of the season, and puts itself in an excellent position in the Big Ten championship race. Who will win Florida vs Texas: Texas -10.5 Have the Florida Gators been "figured out"? I'm not sure. Has Florida had extreme regression over the last few games and probably gotten to a record it should be, even if it required some extremely unbalanced games to do so? Probably so. I'm taking the Texas Longhorns to cover this -10.5 number; it's a small edge, and I wouldn't play it past here. On the other side, the Longhorns' defense ranks 2nd nationally in adjusted EPA per play, 9th against the run and 11th against the pass, while allowing just 29.9% of available yards (5th) . Florida won't trade scores all afternoon. I'll lay it. TOP PICK Florida vs Texas Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 I'm playing the Under 51.5 and would take it down to 50.5 (50%). It's my top pick. The Longhorns rank 5th nationally in early-down EPA per play allowed, which has opponents facing an average 3rd down distance of 8.12 yards , 15th in the country. Florida already ranks 105th in average 3rd down distance at 7.62 yards , so expect a lot of long-yardage situations and stalled drives. Texas also ranks 6th in defensive EPA per drive, so even when the Gators move the ball, points haven't come easily against this unit. The Texas offense isn't built to push this total either. It ranks 55th in success rate and 67th in EPA per pass, and gains just 46.5% of available yards (70th). Expect the Longhorns to win with long, methodical drives that drain the clock rather than quick-strike scores. Florida vs Texas combo This combo is built around one game script: Florida hangs around early, then Texas takes over. Coming off two straight blowouts, the Gators should come out with urgency, and an offense that ranks 8th in EPA per pass can keep them close for a half. Texas's offense isn't built to jump out to fast leads either. The second half is where the Longhorns' advantages show up. Florida's defense ranks dead last in 3rd-and-4th down success allowed, and long Texas drives should wear the Gators down, pull away on the scoreboard, and eat clock to keep this under the total. With a second straight loss to the Gators, Texas would be on the verge of losing any hopes of a spot in the College Football Playoff . But a victory would right the ship for the Longhorns, especially if beleaguered quarterback Arch Manning and an error-prone special teams can trim the mistakes and play a clean game. Under first-year coach Jon Sumrall and breakout running back Jadan Baugh , Florida became one of the early-season darlings of college football after knocking off Ole Miss and climbing into the top 10 of the AP rankings. But the Gators have fallen out of the poll following two straight losses, and a porous Florida defense has given up a combined 83 points over the past two weeks to Missouri and South Carolina. Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Florida Gators. No. 7 Texas (4-1, 1-1 SEC) vs. Florida (4-2, 2-2) When: 11 a.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: Finally, football weather. A Friday cold front drops the temperatures near 50 degrees at kickoff and won't rise much above 70. There may be a few clouds but not much chance of rain. Texas vs Florida football betting info Moneyline: Texas -205, Florida +195 Spread: Texas is favored by 10½ points. Over/under : 52½ Texas history: Florida All-time: Texas leads 3-1-1 Last meeting: Florida 29, Texas 21 (Oct. 4, 2025) Most memorable meeting : Texas 7, Florida 7 (1924). A reported crowd of approximately 10,000 fans filled Clark Field, the current location of the Caven Lacrosse and Sports Center across San Jacinto Boulevard from Royal-Memorial Stadium. The Longhorns held on to the tie by stopping heralded Gator fullback Bill Middlekauff four times inside their own 3-yard line in the final minute of the game. MORE: 'Everything we want is is still right in front of us': Texas football eyes glimmer of hope MORE: Gators QB Aaron Philo uncertain to play due to reported injury Know the foe: Florida Last week: Lost to South Carolina, 38-19 Players to watch: RB Jadan Baugh , a 6-foot-1, 225-pound junior, serves as the centerpiece of the Gator offense. He ranks third in the SEC with 672 yards rushing and leads the conference with 12 rushing touchdowns. In two games against Texas over the past two seasons, he racked up 195 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. QB Aaron Philo , a 6-1, 207-pound junior transfer from Georgia Tech, has been solid if not spectacular, but he may miss the Texas game with an injury . He's thrown for 1,341 yards on 70.5% passing with nine touchdowns and three interceptions and has added 104 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Edge Jayden Woods, a 6-3, 245-pound sophomore, may not quite be at the level of Texas All-American edge Colin Simmons, but he's getting closer. The twitchy pass rusher has 4 ½ sacks and six tackles for a loss, and he'll test the Longhorn pass protection. Central Texas connections: Senior TJ Shananan Jr. , a graduate of Westlake High School in Austin, has started all six games at right guard after spending two seasons at Texas A&M and one year at Penn State. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) When Texas has the ball This seems like a get-right game for Manning, who ranks seventh in the SEC with 224.4 yards a game on 63% passing with 10 touchdowns and five interceptions. Over the past two games against Missouri's Austin Simmons and South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers, Florida's pass defense has allowed a combined 619 yards on 70.8% passing with six touchdown passes and no interceptions. Those two quarterbacks averaged 13.5 yards per completion against the Gators, which could mean lots of action downfield for Texas receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo . Will freshman Derrek Cooper get more snaps at running back for Texas? He showed flashes with a team-high 41 yards rushing against Oklahoma but averages just 3.5 yards per carry for the season. That's even lower than the Longhorns' paltry team average of 3.7 yards a carry. Buoyed by linebacker Myles Graham (41 tackles), the Gators have been respectable against the run while allowing 124.3 yards a game and 3.9 yards a carry. When Florida has the ball Florida won't shy away from the run. It ranks fifth in the SEC with 200.3 yards rushing a game and averages more than 5 yards a carry as a team. Baugh carries the load, but dynamic Duke Clark (265 yards rushing, 7.4 yards per carry) provides an intriguing change of pace. Texas allows just 96 yards rushing a game and 2.8 yards a carry, but linebackers Rasheem Biles (42 tackles) and Justin Cryer (27) are most effective using their speed to chase down backs instead of having to take on linemen. Texas outside corners Bo Mascoe and Kade Phillips have had issues this season, especially when it comes to drawing flags. Florida could test that pair as well as the rest of the secondary if healthy, but that's a big question mark entering Saturday's game. Dallas Wilson (26 catches, 376 yards, three touchdowns) had a breakout game against Texas last season. However, fellow wideout Vernell Brown III has missed the past two games with a knee injury. Brown has 17 receptions for 271 yards and two touchdowns in four games and has also returned two punts for a touchdown. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas vs Florida key matchup Texas center Connor Robertson vs. Florida noseguard Brendan Bett Brendan Bett, a 6-4, 320-pound transfer from Baylor, anchors the interior of the Gators' 3-4 front from his noseguard spot. He's been active with 15 total tackles and three tackles for a loss but doesn't play at the level of the linemen from Oklahoma, Ohio State or Tennessee. If Robertson and guards Dylan Sikorski and Brandon Baker can't clear some running lanes against Bett and the Gators, they may never get the ground game going. Texas vs Florida prediction Thomas Jones: Texas 34, Florida 16. Barring any more special teams disasters or unacceptable turnovers, the Longhorns should have too much firepower for a reeling Florida defense. Danny Davis: Texas. I doubt the offense will have solved all of its problems over the past week, and don't get me started on the special teams. But only minimal improvement from Arch's bunch will be necessary if the Longhorns continue to play well against the run and subdue Jadan Baugh. Cedric Golden: Texas 27, Florida 20. The Horns respond in favorable fashion but questions remain about this offense and its inability to run the ball. Michael Shapiro: Texas 35, Florida 20. Texas coach Steve Sarkisian will get his wish for a fast start with the Longhorns back at Royal-Memorial Stadium, where they enter Saturday eyeing their 24th victory in the last 25 home games. The Florida Gators are in a rough spot at 4-2 as they head to Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns on Saturday afternoon. After two blowout losses to the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks on homecoming, Jon Sumrall 's team is in a tough spot. They were at one point being talked about as potentially being the 2019 LSU Tigers from on the precipice of collapsing. It's his first year at the helm, and the talent level still isn't quite there yet. For the Longhorns, they have beaten Ohio State, but are coming off a tough loss in the Red River Rivalry to the Oklahoma Sooners. They are in an interesting spot right now, and a win is a must for both teams. Who will get the win? Our experts made their predictions. Texas 38, Florida 24 Can we trust the Florida Gators? Honestly, no, and that includes the four-game winning streak to start the season with a massive blowout win over Ole Miss. The defense is struggling to generate pressure and the coverage on the back end has been incredibly inconsistent. Even with Texas having lost Red River last week, their success so far this season and offensive talent gets the Longhorns the win. Can the Gators get the win? Absolutely! Will they? I doubt it. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Texas 33, Florida 19 Both teams come in off dismal losses to unranked teams. The Longhorns, who haven't looked dominant this year by any means, gagged away a game they should have won against Oklahoma but for a pick six and a punt block touchdown. Florida got mollywhopped by South Carolina one game after getting throttled by Missouri. As such, it's tough to tell up from down with these two teams. But my mind immediately goes to two things. First, the Horns' front is still nasty, and Florida suddenly can't find any space for Jadan Baugh and the ground game. On the other side, Florida's defense has become a sieve, and I don't trust they've found a way to fix it yet. Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo are too much for the Longhorns, who win comfortably in Austin. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Texas 31, Florida 20 Arch Manning has faced plenty of criticism for his inconsistency this season, but this is the type of matchup that could help him get back on track. Florida's pass defense has been a major weakness, and I expect Manning to take full advantage by delivering his best performance of the 2026 season. The Longhorns have the talent to exploit the Gators' struggling secondary, and Manning should find plenty of opportunities to push the ball downfield and put points on the board. After an uneven stretch offensively, this could be the breakthrough performance Texas needs. Florida should have some success early, particularly with running back Jadan Baugh leading the way. Baugh has been one of the Gators' most productive playmakers, and I expect him to help Florida move the ball and keep the game competitive in the first half. However, Texas has the defensive talent to make adjustments and limit Florida's offensive production as the game progresses. The Gators have struggled to maintain consistency in recent weeks, and that issue will catch up with them again in Austin. Texas pulls away in the second half, with Manning and the offense doing enough to secure a much-needed win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Texas 21, Florida 17 The Gators have fallen off a bit in the last few weeks after starting red hot. Texas is coming off a disappointing loss to Oklahoma. So, you know, Steve Sarkisian is going to be looking to get his team rolling again. Last week probably showed Texas what they should be doing more often on offense. They need to run more quick-game stuff with Arch Manning, because the long, developing routes downfield aren't helping the offense. Their offensive line isn't great, so they need to start running more quick-game plays. I think this past game showed some of that, and Texas still gets the win despite the offense struggling against a decent Florida defense. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Texas 30, Florida 20 As high as I was on the Florida Gators after the Ole Miss win, that hype has come crashing down after games against Missouri and South Carolina. The offense, led by Jadan Baugh, simply hasn't looked the same, and now the availability of starting QB Aaron Philo is in question. As for Texas, the Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing loss of their own after losing Red River to a bad OU team, and they aim to get back on track. Florida's defense has been bad, to say the least, and this game may serve as a great game for Arch Manning nd Texas. Give me the Longhorns here. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Texas 28, Florida 17 Texas and Florida both need wins this week, and the pressure is even higher for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Two losses for Texas at this point in the season would make things very uncomfortable in Austin, and perhaps it would mark the beginning of the end for some important names there. I don't think that's going to happen, though. I think Texas bounces back this week behind a strong defensive performance and looks the part against Florida. If the Longhorns can limit Jaden Baugh, they'll defend home field without much issue. I think Florida hangs around, but the Longhorns put it away in the fourth quarter. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Texas It shouldn't be much of a surprise that none of our experts have picked the Gators, as they have lost our trust after the disastrous performances of the last two weeks. A win here would do wonders to get them back in our good graces. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Pete Fiutak Wed, October 14, 2026 at 6:42 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just a few weeks ago, Florida was coming off a 52-28 obliteration of a terrific Ole Miss team, and everything was wonderful. The Gators appeared good enough in the first season under Jon Sumrall to be in the SEC and College Football Playoff mix, the offense was unstoppable, and then a funny thing happened. The SEC figured it out. Missouri and South Carolina beat Florida by a combined score of 83-36, and now, with the schedule ahead, the 4-2 team might have to fight just to get to a bowl game. Last week at this time, Texas was No. 1, it was about to play a punchless Oklahoma team, and then a funny thing happened. The Sooners came up with creative and clutch ways to pull off a 27-24 Red River Rivalry win. The season is hardly over for the Longhorns, but now there's little margin for error over a tough second half. Florida vs Texas: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for Florida after this, with a week off before dealing with Georgia, followed up by Oklahoma, and then a trip to Kentucky. Texas starts a run of three straight home games, getting Ole Miss next and Mississippi State to follow. How is this only the sixth game between these two? Texas is 3-1-1, with the 7-7 tie coming in the first meeting in 1924. How To Watch Florida vs Texas Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ABC Location: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin, TX – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Florida Will Win The defense isn't getting fixed over the next few weeks, but that's part of what a rebuild is all about. The Gators win when the offense rocks, and the yards and points allowed are simply the cost of doing business. However, there's one key element to the Florida D that should show up huge. The pass rush is outstanding. The Gator defensive front averages close to three sacks and seven tackles for loss per game, and as good as Arch Manning is – seriously, he's really good, despite the popular opinions at the moment after the OU loss – he's still not amazing when he's getting rushed. The Texas offensive line has been better than last year for the ground game, but the pass protection has been a problem. Why Texas Will Win The Texas defense is going to stuff the Florida offense cold. Missouri and South Carolina never let Gator star Jadan Baugh and the running game breathe. The Gamecocks and Tigers combined for 18 tackles for loss against the Florida attack, and both allowed fewer than 400 yards of total offense. For all the problems in the meltdown against Oklahoma, the Texas defense was great. It allowed only 238 yards of Sooner offense, and for the fourth game in a row – including against Ohio State and Tennessee – the defense allowed fewer than 100 rushing yards. Florida vs Texas Prediction, Betting Lines It turned out to be one of the most important games of the 2025 season. Florida finished the year 4-8, but one of those wins was a 29-21 thriller over Texas. The Longhorns lost on the road to both Ohio State and Georgia – no shame there against two teams that finished with 12 wins – but that loss to the Gators kept them out of the College Football Playoff. Yeah, Texas lost to Oklahoma, but weird things happen in the Red River Rivalry. Against Florida, the offense will keep it conservative, but Arch will connect on a few deep shots to push ahead. The defense will take care of the rest. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:36 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 7 Texas looks to bounce back against Florida after a devastating loss to Oklahoma. Can Arch Manning silence his critics and save the Longhorns' season? No. 7 Texas (4-1) returns home Saturday afternoon to face Florida (4-2) in a massive SEC matchup between two programs desperate for a bounce-back victory. The Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, while Florida was dominated 38-19 at home by South Carolina. Both teams entered the season with championship aspirations, but another loss could seriously damage their College Football Playoff hopes. And for Texas quarterback Arch Manning, the pressure has never been higher. Texas: It's Time for Arch Manning to Deliver Manning entered the season as one of the Heisman Trophy favorites, but his performances have been anything but consistent. Through five games, Manning has thrown for 1,122 yards, 10 touchdowns, and five interceptions. Against Oklahoma, he completed 19 of 31 passes for 260 yards and three touchdowns, but two costly fourth-quarter interceptions helped the Sooners erase a 17-7 halftime deficit. The Longhorns are averaging just 379.2 yards per game, ranking 79th nationally. That's simply unacceptable considering the offensive talent Steve Sarkisian has assembled. However, Saturday presents an excellent opportunity to get things back on track. Florida's defense is allowing 393 yards and 29 points per game, including an alarming 268.7 passing yards per contest. Wide receiver Cam Coleman, who has 318 receiving yards and five touchdowns, should have opportunities to create explosive plays against a struggling Gators secondary. Defensively, Texas has been outstanding, allowing just 16 points and 96 rushing yards per game. Edge rusher Colin Simmons has been nearly unstoppable, recording 9.5 sacks. Florida: Can Jadan Baugh Save the Gators? Florida's offense has actually been impressive this season, averaging 41.7 points and 473.8 yards per game. Quarterback Aaron Philo has thrown for 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns, and three interceptions, while receiver Dallas Wilson has recorded 376 yards and three touchdowns. However, the biggest storyline is running back Jadan Baugh. Baugh has rushed for 672 yards and 12 touchdowns, establishing himself as one of the SEC's most productive backs. Unfortunately, his production has slowed considerably. Over Florida's last two games, Baugh has managed just 72 rushing yards, including 59 yards on 15 carries against South Carolina. That's a major concern considering Texas possesses one of the nation's best rushing defenses. Florida also defeated Texas 29-21 last season, meaning the Gators have already proven they're capable of beating Sarkisian's program. But winning in Austin will be a completely different challenge. How Each Team Wins For Texas, the formula starts with protecting Manning and establishing an early rhythm through the passing game. The Longhorns must take advantage of Florida's vulnerable secondary while allowing their defensive front to disrupt Philo and contain Baugh. For Florida, everything revolves around getting Baugh going early. If the Gators can establish their rushing attack, they'll have opportunities to control possession and keep Manning on the sidelines. Defensively, Florida must force Manning into mistakes, something Oklahoma successfully accomplished last weekend. I expect Texas to respond with a much more disciplined performance following its disappointing loss to Oklahoma. Manning should have opportunities to attack Florida's secondary, but I'm still not convinced he's capable of consistently dominating SEC competition. Expect a solid, rather than spectacular, performance from the Texas quarterback. The biggest difference will be Texas' defense. With Simmons creating pressure and the Longhorns limiting Baugh's rushing opportunities, Florida will struggle to sustain drives throughout the afternoon. I expect the Gators to keep things competitive early, but Texas will gradually take control in the second half. Final Score: No. 7 Texas 27, Florida 17 Texas gets back in the win column, improves to 5-1, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. With the quarterback situation in flux due to Kamario Taylor's apparent turf toe injury sustained against Alabama, State enters the week as two touchdown underdogs on the first fall-like Saturday of football season. Coaches on both sides have a fair amount of familiarity with each other having worked together in Oxford from 2020-21 as boss and apprentice. If Lebby finds a way to get Taylor healthy and ready to roll on Saturday, this may be a barn burner inside Tiger Stadium based on the talent at the offensive skill positions for each team. However, there is a major statistic that isn't being considered in the equation, and that's Kiffin's putrid record against top-25 opponents: 13-26. Mississippi State enters the weeked ranked No. 16 nationally, according to the Week 7 AP Top 25 poll. With an extra week to lick its wounds and recover from a double-digit loss to Alabama, there's a possibility the Bulldogs can find a way to pull off a stunner and keep LSU out of the College Football Playoff entirely in Year 1 under Kiffin. The Bulldogs come in at No. 11 in the SEC, and No. 27 in ESPN's Football Power Index poll with a projected overall record of 8-4 following a 4-1 start on the season. WIth that familiarity, perhaps both coaches feel they understand each other well with tendencies in play calling. "They're really multiple. Zach [Arnett] was with us for a year [at Ole Miss]," Kiffin said Monday. "After Mississippi State, he came over. He's really smart. It's interesting, because he's running a little of his old defense and he's running (Pete) Golding's defense this year. Now, he's even more multiple." picks.headline: LSU vs. Mississippi State Final Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why?
picks.blurb: LSU vs. Mississippi State Final Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB After LSU traveled to Lexington last weekend, Lane Kiffin and the Tigers are coming off of a disappointing loss, heading into the Week 7 matchup against Mississippi State . LSU heads into the matchup with a recent loss, while the Bulldogs are also traveling to Baton Rouge after a loss to the Crimson Tide in Week 5. Before the No. 22 LSU Tigers host the No. 16 Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday, the LSU On SI team predicts which team will win and why. Oct 3, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers safety Tamarcus Cooley (0) intercepts a pass from McNeese Cowboys quarterback Jake Strong (not pictured) during the first half at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ross Abboud The time for sloppiness is over, and everyone in LSU’s football program knows it. Ole Miss was a game you could’ve won. Kentucky was a game you should never have lost. That will be LSU’s wake-up call. LSU 48, Mississippi State 24 Brooke Benedict Unlike last weekend's loss to Kentucky, LSU has to get both sides of the ball to play all four quarters, with the defense able to shut down Mississippi State's pass threat, and Sam Leavitt and his receiver options are able to make key plays during possessions. Without any system errors from the offense, defense and special teams, the team will see some much-needed success back at home, being able to win over the Bulldogs and win back their top-ranked reputation. LSU 33, Mississippi State 21 If Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor plays: Kamario Taylor has an incredible ability to control the long ball, which will force LSU's defense to account for that threat almost all of the time, and following the loss to Kentucky, I expect LSU to play a lot more tight man coverage. The LSU offense, clearly more comfortable playing at home, will establish the run with Dilin Jones against the MSST 3-3-5 defense, and LSU will win a close one late in the 4th. LSU 38, Mississippi State 31 If Taylor doesn't play: If Taylor is unavailable in Saturday's game, the MSST backup QB is not a clear answer. Redshirt Freshman Parker Puckett started in place of Taylor against Alabama, but SEC veteran AJ Swann is also a likely option to play. Regardless, I expect the Bulldogs will be less competitive without the SEC TD leader hurling the rock. LSU wins handily at home. LSU 44, Mississippi State 21 Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor (1) waits for the snap during the third quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Adrian Ramirez Adrian Ramirez LSU will bounce back from its overtime loss to Kentucky with a strong performance at home in Tiger Stadium. If both Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell miss or are limited by their injuries, I expect LSU’s defense to be too much for Mississippi State to handle. I think the Tigers come out with a point to prove and get to work proving it. LSU 31, Mississippi State 14 Hannah Garcia While there’s the possibility of Taylor and Bothwell being out for the game, the LSU defense is still missing key pieces in Spears and Whit Weeks. The receivers have struggled to find consistency all season with catching the ball and Sam Leavitt’s interception numbers are also something that I think could cause LSU to lose. Mississippi State 24, LSU 17 LSU is desperate to bounce back after a tough loss against Kentucky. The keys to this game are Kamario Taylor’s health and Mississippi State’s secondary. Taylor is one of college football’s best quarterbacks, and if he’s not healthy, LSU’s defensive game plan changes. Meanwhile, the Bulldogs allow the second-most passing yards per game in the SEC, so I expect Lane Kiffin to open up the playbook and attack that weakness. I think the Tigers handle business at home. LSU 35, Mississippi State 21 Published 9 hours ago BROOKE BENEDICT Brooke Benedict is a sophomore at LSU, majoring in journalism. Can Lane Kiffin and the Tigers bounce back after an embarrassing loss? The pressure is mounting in Baton Rouge as No. 22 LSU (4-2) prepares to host No. 16 Mississippi State (4-2) Saturday afternoon at Tiger Stadium. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are coming off an embarrassing 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, a game LSU had every opportunity to win before a questionable fourth-down decision allowed the Wildcats to force overtime. Meanwhile, Mississippi State is looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss to Alabama. With LSU already sitting at 1-2 in SEC play, another conference loss could effectively end the Tigers' College Football Playoff hopes. LSU: Can Sam Leavitt Save the Tigers? LSU's offense has shown flashes of brilliance under Kiffin, but consistency remains a major concern. Quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,495 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his eight interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the SEC. Those turnovers have been a major issue for a team that possesses enough offensive talent to compete with nearly anyone. Running back Dilin Jones has provided stability in the backfield, rushing for 426 yards and five touchdowns through LSU's first five games. Wide receiver Winston Watkins Jr. has also emerged as a dangerous weapon, recording 354 receiving yards. Defensively, LSU has been impressive at times, particularly with edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who recorded eight sacks through the team's first five games. However, the Tigers just surrendered 35 points to Kentucky, raising serious questions about their ability to close out games. Against Mississippi State's explosive offense, LSU cannot afford another inconsistent defensive performance. Mississippi State: Kamario Taylor Is a PROBLEM Jeff Lebby has Mississippi State playing some exciting football, and quarterback Kamario Taylor has emerged as one of the SEC's most dangerous young players. Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just four interceptions while completing 66.2% of his passes. However, his availability is a major concern after aggravating a lower-leg injury against Alabama. If Taylor is healthy enough to play, LSU's defense will have its hands full. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has been outstanding, recording 40 receptions for 574 yards and five touchdowns through five games. Running back Fluff Bothwell has also been productive, rushing for 403 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The Bulldogs possess enough offensive firepower to challenge LSU, but their defense remains vulnerable. Mississippi State was allowing 28 points and nearly 380 yards per game through its first five contests. That's a dangerous weakness against a Kiffin-led offense playing at home. How Each Team Wins For LSU, everything starts with protecting the football. Leavitt must avoid costly interceptions and take advantage of Mississippi State's vulnerable secondary. Establishing Jones early should also create opportunities for explosive passing plays. Defensively, LSU needs to pressure Taylor if he plays and prevent Evans from creating big plays downfield. For Mississippi State, the formula revolves around attacking LSU's defense with tempo and forcing Leavitt into mistakes. If Taylor is available, his dual-threat ability could create serious problems. The Bulldogs must also establish Bothwell to prevent LSU from focusing entirely on the passing game. I expect an offensive shootout in Baton Rouge. Mississippi State has enough offensive talent to create problems for LSU, particularly if Taylor is healthy enough to play. However, I believe this is a bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin and the Tigers. Leavitt should have success attacking Mississippi State's secondary, and I expect him to throw for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. The Bulldogs will keep things competitive throughout the afternoon, but LSU's home-field advantage and offensive firepower should ultimately make the difference. Expect Mississippi State to threaten late before LSU's defense comes up with a crucial stop to secure the victory. Final Score: No. 22 LSU 38, No. 16 Mississippi State 31 LSU survives a major scare, improves to 5-2, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. Mandatory Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images (Jordan Prather, IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) 1 / 15 LSU football at Kentucky: Game photos from the sidelines LSU football at Kentucky: Game photos from the sidelines Kamario Taylor's health Kiffin called the Bulldogs' sophomore quarterback a "problem" earlier this week. Kiffin's Ole Miss squad saw Taylor in the regular season finale last year and he and current Ole Miss head coach, then defensive coordinator Pete Golding may still be having visions of Taylor gashing the defense. In that game, Taylor ran for 173 yards and two touchdowns. He nearly rushed for more yards than he threw for; he had 178 passing yards. Ole Miss won the game comfortably, 38-19, but as Kiffin said, Taylor has all the tools to be very problematic for defenses. Mississippi State wasn't able to firmly challenge Alabama at home two weeks ago before the off week. Taylor threw a couple of interceptions and fumbled the ball. So, turnovers were a major issues, but the dual-threat quarterback was also limited in what he could as he's been contending with a lower leg injury. It remains to be seen how healthy Taylor will be, but if he's close to 100%, or fully healthy, this game could be very interesting. Sam Leavitt turnover issues getting perfect matchup? All season to this point, LSU junior starting quarterback Sam Leavitt has had turnover problems. He's the only quarterback in college football that has thrown an interception in every game this year and his eight picks lead FBS. It's a very troubling stat and, if that trend continues, more losses are on the way for the Tigers. But is the Mississippi State defense the perfect matchup for Leavitt? Are the Bulldogs just what the doctor ordered for LSU's gunslinger? So far this season, the Bulldogs have two interceptions and their pass defense is among the worst in the SEC. Mississippi State has also only recovered two fumbles. Good news for Leavitt is Mississippi State doesn't force turnovers. Early kickoff makes LSU's matchup with Mississippi State scarier? The earliest LSU has kicked off a game in the first half of the regular season was 6 p.m. CT. And that was last week. Does that make this 11 a.m. kickoff spot scary for the Tigers welcoming in Mississippi State? The Bulldogs have only played one game so far at 11 a.m., the loss to Alabama. But it also had a 2:30 p.m. kickoff at Minnesota, which they won, 38-13. LSU practiced in the mornings during fall camp and in season. So, to Kiffin, there shouldn't been an adjustment for his team. "I think we'll play really well," Kiffin said earlier this week. "We practice in the morning every day. So they're up doing that. It's really more what their clock is. I used to be more concerned when we went to this format of the night games being opposite of their body clock. So I don't see it being an issue." LSU football offensive line play LSU struggled to find traditional balance on offense at Kentucky last week. The Wildcats don't have an awesome rush defense, but were able to keep Tiger running backs Dilin Jones and Harlem Berry from getting much of anything going. They combined for 60 rushing yards. Mississippi State's rush defense has fared better so far this season than Kentucky's has, allowing almost 16 yards on the ground less. The Bulldogs have given up five rushing scores on the season. The play up front from LSU's offense must be better this week for the team to keep the Bulldogs at bay. LSU sports the third best running attack in the SEC at 213 yards per game, but Leavitt has played a large role in that and he leads the team in rushing scores with seven. LSU's offensive line need to open run lanes for Jones and Berry against Mississippi State. LSU vs Mississippi State prediction The last time LSU lost under Kiffin a few weeks ago, it was able to bounce back at home and take care of business. Quarterback Kamario Taylor in head coach Jeff Lebby's high-flying offense poses a legit threat to any defense. And this game being an 11 a.m. kickoff also feels like a prime disaster spot for the Tigers. This game will be high scoring, but the question is: which defense will find enough stops to seal the win? I think LSU gets a couple more stops than Mississippi State's defense that averages giving up almost 40 points a game in SEC play. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs will face off against the Auburn Tigers in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry on Saturday afternoon. The weather forecast calls for a beautiful fall Saturday, where the high in Athens is supposed to be just 67 degrees. The betting forecast is calling for the Dawgs to beat the Tigers by about three touchdowns. This will likely not be a close game, which means we can be a little looser with our bold predictions for it. Here are three bold ones for Kirby Smart and Alex Golesh’s first game in this rivalry: Georgia has a 100-Yard Rusher and Receiver The Dawgs can take advantage of this Auburn defense, which is a bottom half unit in the conference, allowing over 350 yards of total offense per game. Georgia’s offense has been extremely productive, ranking top three in the conference. Georgia having a back and a wideout go for 100 yards in the same game hasn’t happened in 10 years. So, yeah. This is a bold prediction. I think about a guy like Talyn Taylor or Craig Dandridge, who have hit on some explosive passing plays. All it takes is one or two of those and some screens and underneath throws to work for that 100-yard game to come into play. Auburn is also among the worst rushing defenses in the SEC. We saw Dwight Phillips Jr. run for over 100 yards against Alabama on just 17 carries. He, Nate Frazier and Bo Walker have each registered multiple explosive runs. All it takes is for one of them to bust a huge run and that 100-yard mark is well within reach. Dawgs go for 250 On the Ground Auburn is allowing about 150 yards per game on the ground. I think Georgia could go for over 250. They have done it twice already and ran for over 200 yards in two other games. Auburn allowed almost 250 yards to both Tennessee and Florida. Georgia has a better offense than both of those teams. The Dawgs could really blow Auburn out on Saturday, and if they do that then there will be a lot of yards gained on the ground. Partially due to garbage time. Georgia Holds Auburn to Under 300 Total Yards Auburn has possibly the most unique offense that Georgia will see all year. There is an argument to be made that the Dawgs will struggle more in this game than you would initially think because of that. Auburn takes the least amount of time in between plays and runs more options and designed quarterback run plays than any other offense that Georgia will see this year. I am not buying it. Georgia’s defense has been the best in college football. The Dawgs will shut down Auburn on Saturday. picks.blurb: Auburn @ Georgia Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Auburn @ Georgia Preview And Prediction Oct 10, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) directs teammate running back Nick Peal (30) during the third quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 1 Georgia hosts Auburn in the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. No, it's not nearly as fierce as the Iron Bowl when Alabama takes on Auburn, but when you've played 130 times, you tend to have a few interesting moments that build into something generational. Georgia just got by Alabama in a controversial 20-17 thriller – let's just say the Bulldogs got a wee bit of a break on a key Crimson Tide deep shot – and now it's the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn has had two weeks off to get ready for this, and knocking the Bulldogs off of their lofty perch would put the first season under head coach Alex Golesh into hyperdrive. Auburn vs Georgia: Quick Hits Auburn gets LSU and the Lane Kiffin show next, and then goes to Ole Miss. Georgia gets a week off before playing the Cocktail Party showdown against Florida in Atlanta, and then it goes to Ole Miss. Georgia has won seven times in the series since losing in 2017 (it was No. 1 in the nation then, too), but it won the SEC Championship a few weeks later. The Bulldogs have won 11 of the last 12 meetings. It might have been hit hard by Florida, but it does a lot of bending without breaking, thanks to plenty of sacks, lots of plays behind the line, and a third down defense that's holding up well. Offensively, the high-tempo Tiger attack should be able to keep the Bulldogs on their heels. Alabama ran well last week, but it only handed the ball off 29 times. Auburn won't make that mistake, pushing for at least 35 carries, and close to 40, as it tries to hit the Georgia defense with tempo. Why Georgia Will Win Georgia's defensive front will live in the Auburn backfield. It's a problem with Auburn's style that it allows defenses to tee off on the quarterback and come up with too many tackles for loss. The Tigers don't worry about the time of possession battle, and they're good at overcoming negative plays with something positive, but Georgia has the defense to swarm all over the quick-hitting short plays. Auburn doesn't do anything deep, and Georgia should limit any yards after the catch or runs that get to the second level. Auburn vs Georgia Prediction, Betting Lines It's been an interesting start to the Golesh era. The offense is supposed to dominate and take over, but it doesn't do it enough. The defense that was so great last year has stayed strong, but it's about to get pounded on. Auburn's two losses came when it allowed over three yards per carry. Georgia is averaging over six yards per pop. Georgia has 6 players listed on the latest report, updated most recently on Thursday, Oct. 15. That doesn't include running back Nate Frazier, but does include safety KJ Bolden. Running back Chauncey Bowens (lower body) Wide receiver Isiah Canion (leg). Outside linebacker Amaris Williams (knee). Wide receiver Thomas Blackshear (collarbone).

away.headline: Auburn vs. Georgia early injury report: Who's in, who's out
away.blurb: The Tigers emerge from the bye week relatively healthy, with only two players, tight end Hunter Herring and offensive lineman Tai Buster, ruled out for Saturday's game at Georgia due to injury. However, the biggest news from the initial report is that linebacker Xavier Atkins is officially ruled out. Auburn Tigers — OUT: LB Xavier Atkins, TE Hunter Herring, OL Tai Buster Georgia Bulldogs — OUT: WR Thomas Blackshear, RB Chauncey Bowens, WR Isiah Canion, LB Amaris Williams, S Tyriq Green; Questionable: DB KJ Bolden; Probable: OL Marcus Harrison Atkins, who is tied for the team lead in sacks and second on the team in tackles, has been suspended for Saturday's game at No. 1 Georgia, according to Auburn head coach Alex Golesh. Golesh first mentioned the suspension during Monday's press conference and clarified Wednesday that Atkins is not with the team during practice this week. Golesh will address Atkins' status again next week. The Bulldogs will be without several players, including running back Chauncey Bowens, who leads the team in rushing touchdowns with six. However, Georgia received potentially good news on Wednesday as running back Nate Frazier is not on the availability report after missing four straight games with a rib injury. He was not included on the availability report for Georgia's Week 6 game at Alabama ; however, he did not play. away.headline: Georgia Injury Report Ahead of Auburn Game Reveals Troubling Reality with RB Room
away.blurb: As it turns out though, Kirby Smart's team is going to be a little bit banged up as they try to avoid a first home defeat against Auburn in more than two decades. As was the case last week, the running back room is going to be a bit thin. With the reporting around Chauncey Bowens as murky as ever, he has been ruled out for the second straight week and could wind up missing more time than that. Bowens is ruled out along with Isiah Canion, who has not seen much work this season. Thomas Blackshear is also out once again, but this is not a huge surprise. The bigger surprising thing is KJ Bolden being listed as questionable, potentially banged up from the Alabama game but dealing with an unknown injury. Reports from Pete Thamel of ESPN indicated that while Nate Frazier is not on the injury report, he was not last week either but still did not end up playing in the win over Alabama. Regardless, it looks like it could be a significant opportunity once again for guys like Dwight Phillips Jr. and Bo Walker to tote the rock and showcase the depth that Georgia has at the position. Given what the Dawgs proved against the Crimson Tide, they should be able to run the ball with success once again versus Auburn even without Bowens and likely Frazier as well. As Georgia tries to stay undefeated and keep the winning streak against Auburn alive, there is going to be serious urgency from this team to play as well as they did last week, which can often be difficult to replicate. If Gunner Stockton can keep up his strong level of play, this Dawgs team is going to be tough for anyone they face to have a real chance of winning. Once again though, he is going to be doing it with a little bit of a shorthanded running back room. As for what that means moving forward for the rest of the season, it remains to be seen, but Georgia certainly passed the first test with a depleted running back room. Time will tell if they can pass the next one as well.

away.headline: Georgia football injury report: KJ Bolden downgraded heading into Auburn game
away.blurb: While offensive lineman Marcus Harrison was removed from the report, Georgia safety KJ Bolden was downgraded from questionable to doubtful. Defensive back Tyriq Green (ankle) — out Outside linebacker Amaris Williams (knee) — out Wide receiver Thomas Blackshear (shoulder) — out Wide receiver Isiah Canion (right leg) — out Running back Chauncey Bowens (lower leg) — out Safety KJ Bolden (right leg) — doubtful Other possibilities include Zion Branch, Ja’Marley Riddle and Blake Stewart. Green would also be worth monitoring but he is out once again after suffering an ankle injury against Western Kentucky. Nate Frazier is once again absent from the availability report for Georgia, indicating he’s able to play. That was the case last week, before Frazier was held out of Georgia’s win over Alabama. Dwight Phillips ran for 120 yards while Bo Walker added another 69 on the ground. But with Bowens and Dante Dowdell both out for Georgia, it will be worth monitoring if Frazier sees the field. Georgia is a nearly three-touchdown favorite against the visiting Auburn Tigers. The Bulldogs also have an off week coming out of this game. The SEC will put out another availability report on Friday, before providing a final update 90 minutes before kickoff. He has 22 tackles, 2 pass breakups, 2.0 tackles for loss and an interception. He led Georgia in snaps played against Alabama. In the event he doesn’t play , Georgia does have options in the secondary. The Bulldogs could slide Rasean Dinkins over and play he and Kyron Jones at safety. Doing so would allow Georgia to keep Khalil Barnes at the star position. The Clemson transfer has excelled in that role for Georgia this season. The Bulldogs have looked like a team that is in store for a long season with how the first six weeks have gone. If they are to accomplish all of their goals this season, it will need Bolden and Frazier healthy and contributing at the end of the season. Saturday’s game is set for a 3:30 p.m. ET start.

home.headline: Injury Report: Kirby Smart is Right to be Concerned About "Banged Up" Georgia Football
home.blurb: UGA RB Chauncey Bowens, WR Isiah Canion and Auburn transfer and UGA DL Amaris Williams are all listed as “out” on Wednesday night’s SEC injury report that schools are mandated to complete by conference rule. Amaris Williams has been out for some time, and was never expected to play in this contest, but his status as well as that of Bowens and Canion backs up coach Kirby Smart’s comments after the 20-17 win over Alabama Saturday night. “We're a beat-up football team right now,” Smart said at Bryant-Denny Stadium . “We have guys out left and right, and to have both those backs out and Isiah (Canion) out at receiver - tough deal, but we responded.” One of those two backs that didn’t play Saturday night was not on the injury report Wednesday night, either. Nate Frazier has only played a handful of snaps since Georgia’s lopsided win at Arkansas . He was listed as questionable for two weeks, and played sparingly against Vanderbilt. There was some other news for the Dawgs in the injury report. Star DB KJ Bolden is listed as questionable for the game Satuday against the Tigers. The Bulldogs are starting to get thin in the secondary as well as fellow safety Tyriq Green is listed as out for the game. Injury Report: Kirby Smart is Right to be Concerned About "Banged Up" Georgia Football Skip to main content SI.COM ATHENS - Three players thought to be major contributors to Georgia football’s 2026 season will not play against the Auburn Tigers this weekend. Frazier was not listed in the injury report last week at all, but did not play at Alabama - meaning the Dawgs were down two of their top three running backs for the huge showdown with the Crimson Tide. It gave Dwight Phillips a massive opportunity to step up, and he did. “What a great kid, man. This Dwight Phillips, man, y'all don't know how special this kid is,” Smart said after the win over Alabama . “He hasn’t complained one time since being here, and he's so tough for his size. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Alabama looks to recover from its first loss of the season on Saturday at No. 14 Tennessee Getty Images A pair of historic rivals with playoff aspirations are squaring off in a top-15 SEC showdown on Saturday, as No. 6 Alabama travels to No. 14 Tennessee for the Third Saturday in October. The Crimson Tide will be looking to avoid losing consecutive regular season games for the first time since 2007, while the Volunteers will be seeking to snap a four-game home losing streak against ranked opponents. Alabama (5-1, 3-1 SEC) took a 20-17 home loss to Georgia last week, which leaves the Crimson Tide with a dwindling margin for error entering the second half of their schedule. Tennessee (5-1, 2-1) is coming off an ugly 24-17 win at Arkansas in need of the resume boost that would come with knocking off Alabama. While Tennessee's defense is thriving midway through the season, facing Alabama will be its toughest test yet. Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell leads the league in passing yards with 1,599 and brings game-changing mobility. Though Alabama star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is expected to miss the game due to injury, Bama's offense will still pack a punch that tests Tennessee's secondary. The Volunteers counter with the nation's No. 15 rushing offense and a languishing passing attack that will need to get better if they are going to pull an upset that would reverberate through the SEC and beyond. With blowout road wins over quality foes Kentucky and Mississippi State already in hand, the Tide will look to keep rolling on the road with their first win in Knoxville since 2020. Alabama vs. Tennessee: Need to know Neyland blues: The last time Tennessee beat a ranked team at Neyland Stadium was in 2024, when it edged No. 7 Alabama 24-17. The Vols finished 0-3 at home against ranked opponents last season and fell 20-17 to Texas in Week 4, extending their home losing streak against ranked opponents to four games. But something will have to give as the Crimson Tide have dropped two straight inside Neyland Stadium. Whichever team is smoking, the traditional postgame victory cigars will hit a little different this time. Tennessee's QB question: Tennessee sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre made his first career start last week in the Volunteers' 24-17 win at Arkansas, stepping in for injured and underperforming freshman Faizon Brandon . Now the question is how long the Volunteers will stick with MacIntyre, who completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions against the Razorbacks. Regardless of who gets the nod against Alabama, the Crimson Tide's priority will be to slow down the SEC's second-leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , and to make Tennessee's fledgling passing attack prove that it can deliver. Playoff implications: With a win, Alabama will have an 87.7% chance of reaching the College Football Playoff, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. A loss would drop that mark to 52.9% and crush Alabama's margin for error. Because the Crimson Tide's strength of schedule lags behind others in the SEC, its case for inclusion as a three-loss team would be shaky. Tennessee's playoff odds would shoot to 51.6% with a win and drop to 16.8% with a loss. Replicating that formula against Alabama won't be possible unless the Crimson Tide shoot themselves in the foot with turnovers and special team miscues. Because the Crimson Tide won't respect the Volunteers' passing game, they'll be able to load the box and frustrate Tennessee's ground game, much like Texas did in Week 4. Offensively, Alabama has too much firepower to be fully restrained for four quarters. Look for Bama to pull away in the fourth quarter. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs Tennessee: Alabama -7.5 If last week was any indicator, Tennessee has far more problems than Alabama , despite the Volunteers' win and the Crimson Tide's loss. In George MacIntyre's first start for Josh Heupel, he finished with just a 10.3 QBR in a seven-point win against Arkansas. He'll be starting again against Bama, which is why I like the Tide to cover -9.5 or better . Arkansas lost to its previous three Power Four opponents by an average of 29.3 points, including a 28-point defeat to Georgia — the same team Alabama lost to by just three on the road last week. Tennessee's offense won't be able to keep up with Alabama. Keelon Russell ranks third nationally in QBR (90.0) , and the Tide are top 20 in offensive success rate (50.1%). His dual-threat ability has helped open up the run game, too, with Alabama ranking fourth nationally in rush success rate (53.3%) . That won't cut it against an Alabama defense tied for the 14th-most sacks in the country (17). I'm expecting a fast start from Russell after last week's tough loss to Georgia, and once Bama takes the lead, Tennessee isn't equipped to come back with MacIntyre behind center. Following their loss to Georgia a week ago, the Crimson Tide head to Knoxville looking to get back on track. In this classic SEC showdown, I've found a few player props worth dabbling in, including another big outing from Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell. Without further ado, here are my Alabama vs. Tennessee prop picks . Before you get too far, be sure to check out all of our college football picks for Week 7. Best Alabama vs Tennessee props Prop pick #1: Keelon Russell Over 240.5 Pass Yards (53.27%) Alabama star sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell should be amped up to bounce back after an underwhelming 16-for-30, 185-yard performance with just one touchdown in the Crimson Tide's loss to Georgia. That said, it came against arguably the best defense in the country. It was Russell's worst performance since throwing for just 188 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Week 2 against Kentucky. Over six games this season, Russell still averages more than this prop at 266.5 passing yards per game. He draws a Tennessee defense that has shut down quarterbacks all season, allowing just 185 passing yards per game. However, what elite quarterback have the Volunteers actually shut down? "Well, they held Arch Manning to just 201 yards." Oh, like that holds up in the year of our Lord 2026. Russell is far better than Manning and has faced far tougher competition this season than what this Volunteers pass defense has seen. Coming off a matchup against one of the country's best defenses, the sophomore should clear 240 passing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 250.5 passing yards. Prop pick #2: DeSean Bishop Over 89.5 Rush Yards (50.74%) With Tennessee's run-heavy offense averaging nearly 43 rushing attempts per game this season, I don't expect that approach to change on Saturday against a very talented Alabama run defense. Over their last three games against Texas, Auburn, and Arkansas, the Volunteers still average 38.33 attempts per game . Tennessee should lean on its leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , to move the ball downfield . Last week against Georgia, this Crimson Tide defense showed some flaws when junior running back Dwight Phillips Jr. rushed for 120 yards on just 17 carries . That's the same number of carries Bishop averages per game this season, and Alabama is coming off a game where it struggled to stop the run. Bishop is averaging 113 yards per game and more than six yards per carry this season. If he gets his usual workload, he should be in a great spot to record 90-plus rushing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 95+ yards. Prop pick #3: Keelon Russell Over 24.5 Rush Yards (53.49%) I gave out this same prop last week, so I'll start this one the same way: If you can secure Russell's longest rush over 15.5 yards , take it! Russell has surpassed that mark in every game this season. Plus, the longest rush prop eliminates the possibility of sacks taking away rushing yards, so if you can access it, take it Over his standard rushing yards prop at 25+. However, Russell has still rushed for Over 25 yards in four of his six games this season . The sophomore quarterback is averaging 7.66 rushing attempts per game, and with the Crimson Tide likely to be leading, as the spread indicates, they'll eventually want to chew some clock. That should give Russell plenty of chances to rack up yards on the ground. The last mobile quarterback Tennessee faced was Auburn's Byrum Brown, who averages 16.2 rushing attempts per game and racked up more than 107 rushing yards against the Volunteers. Russell just needs 25 and should have plenty of opportunities on Saturday. Take this up to 30+ rushing yards. TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 10: Head coach Kalen DeBoer of the Alabama Crimson Tide reacts to a play during the second half of the game against the Georgia Bulldogs at Bryant Denny Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Butch Dill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brent Taylor Sun, October 11, 2026 at 5:39 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After a close loss to Georgia, Alabama didn't drop in the Coaches Poll Rankings , hanging in at number 7. Essentially, Alabama proved they belong with the elite teams, with a resume boasting a win over the suddenly excellent Kentucky and a loss to #1 Georgia that could have gone either way. The Tennessee Volunteers are similarly 5-1, but it took squeaking out tight wins over SEC bottom feeders Arkansas and Auburn. The Vols have generally played well on defense, but their offense has left a LOT to be desired, with QB Faizon Brandon leading an anemic passing attack until he was injured, and backup George MacIntyre not doing any better. So they're sitting put with a #15 ranking. FanDuel's sportsbook has the opening odds set to Alabama holding a -6.5 favorite over Tennessee, with an over/under of 55.5. Week 1 – Beat Furman 56-9 Week 2 – Beat Georgia Tech 45-24 Week 3 – Beat Kennesaw State 42-9 Week 4 – Lost to Texas 17-20 Week 5 – Beat Auburn 24-14 Week 6 – Beat Arkansas 24-17 The Vols are averaging 22 points per game on offense and 17 points per game on defense in SEC play, with the biggest problem being that, for the season, they're averaging only 187 passing yards per game (and that includes their three warm up games to start the season). Running back DeSean Bishop is still carrying the entire offense with 678 rushing yards. Week 1 – Beat East Carolina 48-10 Week 2 – Beat Kentucky 45-17 Week 3 – Beat Florida State 50-36 Week 4 – Beat South Carolina 49-18 Week 5 – Beat Mississippi State 56-23 Week 6 – Lost to Georgia 17-20 The Tide's offense obliterated all of their first five foes, scoring 45+ in every single game despite having only a single cupcake game. Then Georgia happened, and the two elite squads turned the game into a low-possession, high-stakes contest (seriously, there were only 7 combined drives in the entire second half). The Alabama defense has had some struggles this year. They've been a playmaking defense, but they've also given up some downfield passes in almost every game, and then struggled with UGA's rushing attack last week. Still, the held the Dogs to less than half of their usual offensive output. Alabama boasts a much better offense, but the two teams have likely equivalent defenses. However, the game will be at Neyland Stadium. Still, the 6.5 spread with a 55.5 OU has the prediction something like a 31-25 Crimson Tide victory. How the Tide responds to a tough and disappointed loss in their clash with Georgia will be paramount, but I wouldn't be surprised if this one winds up going under the 55.5 points. Something more like a 21-14 kind of game. What do you think? Give us your thoughts in the comments below.

away.headline: 3 crucial questions for Alabama to answer in Tennessee game
away.blurb: UA’s starting center, Delgatty was listed as doubtful on Thursday’s availability report. If he can’t go, Mal Waldrep is set to step in at center, after he took over for his injured teammate against Georgia. On the other side of the ball, UA’s defensive line was already depleted with Jeremiah Beaman out. On Saturday, Terrance Green reaggravated a previous injury, and will miss the Tennessee matchup. Early in the week it became clear that one of Alabama’s top playmakers was going to miss the trip to Knoxville. Ryan Coleman-Williams was already dealing with injuries before taking a head-to-head hit against Georgia, and was declared out on the first availability report of the week. “We learn from this week and we go bring the same energy we had last Tuesday, the Tuesday before that and the excitement and understanding that we get to go do this. Like, this is what you wanted. This is what you came here for. Let’s make the most of them. Take advantage of the opportunity to go out there and play in an awesome environment that’s going to be there on Saturday, and now we just gotta go prepare for it.” One week after a tough loss to Georgia, Alabama football returns to SEC play on Saturday. The Crimson Tide faces a tough trip to Tennessee , with both teams entering the game with 5-1 records. The game is scheduled to kick off at 2:30 p.m. CT Saturday at Neyland Stadium. Before the Third Saturday in October game, here are three questions for Alabama to answer. Can the Crimson Tide overcome injuries up front? While Ryan Coleman-Williams’ head injury made for the most headlines from the Georgia game, the Crimson Tide might have had more impactful injuries on its lines. On offense, it was Racin Delgatty who went down, with a lower leg injury. The Crimson Tide will need to hope for no further injuries up front. If someone else goes down, the rest of Alabama’s backups have far less experience. Can the Crimson Tide get the quality snaps it needs from less proven players on the lines? Who will step up at wide receiver? The Crimson Tide will need to make plays elsewhere if it is to beat the Volunteers. Lotzier Brooks has already proven himself, while Rico Scott, Noah Rogers, Cederian Morgan and Derek Meadows will all be fighting for reps as well. “We’ve got a group of really competitive players,” Noah’s really progressing. We think he’s really pretty close to 100% now. And Derek Meadows is showing up, he made a nice play at the end of the game there, obviously. “So we’re lucky to have that many guys. home.headline: Alabama dealt unfortunate injury news ahead of Tennessee clash
home.blurb: The Alabama Crimson Tide will look to bounce back after a razor close loss to the Georgia Bulldogs in Week 6 when they face off against the Tennessee Volunteers. But unfortunately, they will not be at full strength offensively in Saturday’s game. Junior wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams has been one of the more reliable and effective wide receivers in all of college football this season for the Crimson Tide. Prior to their loss to Georgia, Coleman-Williams had put together a three-game streak of finding the end zone at least once. During their Week 6 loss to Georgia, Coleman-Williams was forced to exit the game after both seemingly re-aggravating a knee injury in the game and suffering a concussion, which was what ultimately cut his game in Week 6 short. More news : Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor Vows to ‘Ruin’ LSU’s Night Leading up to the team’s Week 7 game, there was not much optimism that Coleman-Williams was going to be able to suit up for the game. And that reality was confirmed on Wednesday when Alabama released their weekly injury report, along with a report on the matter from Pete Nakos of On3 Sports. More news : UCLA HC Bob Chesney Drops Powerful Quote After Bruins’ Hot Start Considering Coleman-Williams leads the team in every major statistical category, including receptions (tied with Lotzeir Brooks), receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns, his absence on Saturday will almost certainly be missed. Add in the fact that the Tennessee Volunteers allow just 161.3 passing yards per game to opposing teams, the second-lowest passing yards allowed to opponents in the SEC, and it could very well be a tough day for Alabama star quarterback Keelon Russell. Saturday’s Alabama-Tennessee matchup will kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC.
