picks.headline: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why?
picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Somewhat quietly, one of the bigger games on college football slate this weekend is happening at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium between No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) and No. 13 Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). Both squads enter with one loss and need a win this weekend to maintain a reasonable path to the College Football Playoffs. However, alongside the high-stakes of the matchup are the storylines revolving around each team’s roster. Rebels’ star running back Kewan Lacy will be facing his former team for the first time since leaving Missouri, following his true freshman season in 2024. Meanwhile, former Ole Miss starters Austin Simmons, Cayden Lee and Chris Graves Jr. all return to Oxford for the first time since they entered the transfer portal, following the Rebels’ deep run through last year’s playoffs. Saturday’s kickoff between the Rebels and Tigers is set for 2:30 p.m. CT on the SEC Network. Ole Miss entered the week as six-point home favorites. Ahead of the Rebels' latest pressure-filled matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Sep 26, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Pete Golding looks on after an interception against the Florida Gators during the second half at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis Welcome to the gauntlet that is the College Football Playoffs….or at least the very real warmup version of it. The loser of this weekend’s game in Oxford isn’t mathematically out of the 12-team race, but it’s going to be a loss that will be immensely hard to overcome looking at Ole Miss’ and Missouri’s schedule. As far as the actual matchup is concerned, going into the game, Missouri has played better on the defensive side of the ball and matches the Rebels’ offensive firepower with Austin Simmons and Jamal Roberts leading the way. The Tigers’ rush attack could have the ability to give the Rebels a long afternoon, and we’ll really find out if Ole Miss improved enough from its nightmare performance defending the run against Florida. Ole Miss doesn’t have to completely shut down Mizzou’s ground game, it more than likely won’t, but if it can limit Roberts and the rest of the production in the backfield, the Rebels should give themselves a real chance at picking up a critical win. In my mind, that’s going to be the key to victory for Ole Miss. I believe this game will come down to the final few possessions and whichever offense has the ball last in that scenario. Given the large sample size we’ve seen of Trinidad Chambliss in those types of situations, I have a hard time picking against those results. Ole Miss 34, Missouri 31 Matt Galatzan All of the talk is going to be about the return of Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee to Oxford, and Kewan Lacy facing off against his former team. However, there needs to be more talk about Missouri's defense, or more specifically, its pass rush. The Tigers have 18 sacks this year, which is tied with Texas for third in the SEC behind LSU and Tennessee. Meanwhile, the Rebels are No. 1 in the SEC in sacks allowed with just five. If the Rebels can protect Trinidad Chambliss and slow down a balanced Missouri offense, they will be in good shape. I think they do both just enough to get the win. Ole Miss 30, Missouri 27 I think Ole Miss will take home a hard-fought victory against former Rebels’ quarterback Austin Simmons, wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. and the rest of the Missouri Tigers. Simmons, Lee and running back Jamal Roberts are likely to give head coach Pete Golding and his defense trouble, leading to a “bend-don’t-break” type of performance, following a bounce-back game against Vanderbilt for the Rebels’ defense. However, I’m comfortable predicting Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, wide receiver Deuce Alexander and running back Kewan Lacy to outplay Simmons, Lee and Roberts and give the Rebels a high-scoring ranked win in Ole Miss’ homecoming game. Ole Miss 38, Missouri 31 Zion Trammell Ole Miss and Missouri feature star-studded quarterbacks in Trinidad Chambliss and Austin Simmons. This has the makings of a high-scoring affair, so whichever quarterback can protect the ball better could decide the outcome. I think Chambliss and Kewan Lacy play their best games of the year, and Ole Miss gets by with a win. Ole Miss 31, Missouri 28 Cooper Ferguson Back in the Vaught, I want to see a great response to the blowout victory in Nashville. All will go well if Trinidad Chambliss plays as he has so far. After a second-half respite in the Vanderbilt game, Kewan Lacy is primed for a breakout game in the 2026 campaign. I fear the talent and connection between Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee, but I do not see the Rebels dropping a game at VHS this season. Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. Here's what Mizzou fans need to know about the Rebels, from their starting quarterback to their top playmakers, as well as a score prediction for the Week 7 game: Mizzou has 3 players from Ole Miss CFP roster, including QB Austin Simmons Anyone with a passing interest is aware: Austin Simmons is among three MU players going back to face their former team, along with wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. Simmons' situation is a little different. He's going to duke it out against the quarterback who took his starting job last season. Trinidad Chambliss was one of the stories of the season in 2025, leading Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff semifinals in his first season after transferring up from Division-II Ferris State. But the thing with Cinderella tales in sports … someone has to lose. That was Simmons, who began last year as the Rebels' starter. He's been widely praised in Oxford for how he handled the change and, essentially, a benching. He sustained an ankle injury in Week 2 and never got his job back. All's well that ends well. Simmons has found new life as the starter at Missouri and is beginning to generate some first-round NFL Draft interest. Chambliss is back in college because of an offseason court case that revolved around a medical redshirt during his time at Ferris State. Mizzou has a tough job defending Chambliss, who is currently fourth in the betting odds for the Heisman Trophy. He's mobile, has a tremendous arm and doesn't take too many sacks. Missouri has a dangerous offense, too, with Simmons and Lee leading the group. The winner is rewarded with a clearer path to making the CFP this year. "I wish them a lot of luck," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said Oct. 12, "other than this week when we're playing against them." More: Missouri football's biggest test yet comes in star Trinidad Chambliss More: Why Eli Drinkwitz isn't concerned with Ole Miss' familiarity with Austin Simmons How much does Kewan Lacy elevate Ole Miss offense? Speaking of reunions … Kewan Lacy started his career at Mizzou in 2024. He was a reserve behind Nate Noel and Marcus Carroll. He transferred to Ole Miss after his rookie year, which — talk about sliding doors moments — was among the reasons the Tigers added Ahmad Hardy out of the portal. Hardy and Lacy were Nos. 1 and 2 in the SEC for rushing yards last year, respectively, so the move worked out just fine for all parties. It'll be Lacy vs. Jamal Roberts on Saturday out of the backfield. Roberts currently leads the Power-conferences with 828 rushing yards. Lacy has been dealing with a shoulder injury and missed much of the start of this season. He returned this past Saturday in Ole Miss's win at Vandy with seven carries for 39 yards and a touchdown. Ole Miss's running numbers on the box score are modest, but the analytics paint a much prettier picture. The Rebels' rushing success rate of 60.7% ranks 10th nationally, per Hudl IQ. Every time they run the ball, they're generating 0.16 in 'Expected Points Added,' which is in the top five in the SEC (Missouri's EPA per rush is 0.05). A fully healthy Lacy can only help that cause. He forced 89 missed tackles last season, a number only bested by Hardy. He led the nation with 24 touchdowns. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Ole Miss run defense has struggled So, Ole Miss's offense looks pretty good. The defense, however … The Rebels are allowing 392.4 yards per game, which is the second-most in the SEC. The kicker — Ole Miss is giving up 176.4 yards per game on the ground. That's the worst in the conference by quite some distance. Opponents' rushing success rate against Ole Miss is above 50%, per Hudl IQ, which means offenses are staying on schedule with more than half of their rushing attempts against the Rebels. Only Florida, which Mizzou gashed for 220 yards on the ground, Arkansas and Vanderbilt have defended the run worse in the SEC. Teams are generating runs of 15 or more yards 5.6% of the time against Ole Miss and runs of 30 or more yards 3.1% of the time. The Rebels have given up explosives. Roberts just became the third running back in the SEC in the last 20 years to run for 200 or more yards in back-to-back FBS games. The Tigers are committed to the run game, and unless Ole Miss has found a week-to-week fix, they should find some opportunities for Roberts to get loose. Missouri Tigers running back Jamal Roberts (20) celebrates with offensive lineman Tristan Wilson (73) after scoring against the Texas A&M Aggies during the second half of the game at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium on Oct. 10, 2026. Score prediction: Missouri 41, Ole Miss 38 When I wrote a game-by-game prediction on Aug. 29 before the season, I wrote the following about Mizzou's trip to Ole Miss: "Something about this game just feels like it's going to get weird. Break containment." I have not moved off of that prediction. My chaos radar is going berserk. I am, however, changing who I think will win. Ole Miss does not seem particularly adept at stopping the run. Roberts is not the back you want to see when you're struggling to contain chunk plays. The outside zone and fist fight it creates is not the scheme you want to work out the problems against. Mizzou's defense has been tremendous, but Ole Miss is going to score. The Rebels are too good not to. Our pregame prediction just has Missouri scoring more. (5-1) headed to Oxford, MS for a battle with the #9 Ole Miss Rebels (4-1). Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 last week following the bye week and couldn’t have looked more crisp. Missouri on the other hand smoldered Texas A&M 27-6 and ran for more yards (247) than the Aggies had as an offense (216). Missouri is 7-1 all-time against Ole Miss as the last meeting was in 2019. Ole Miss’ lone win in the series came in 1974, 10-0! We can surely expect more than 10 points in this game as both offenses looked good last week. Missouri has ran for 467 yards and five touchdowns over the last two weeks with Jamal Roberts totaling 433 of those yards and all five scores. Ahmad Hardy has not returned to practice, so it’s been an opportunistic year for Roberts. This game is also a headliner quarterback Austin Simmons following his transfer from Ole Miss. Simmons has been fantastic for Missouri. He has a 14:1 TD to INT ratio after tossing his first pick of the season last week, plus a 64.8 completion percentage and 1,474 yards. Simmons was injured at Ole Miss and never saw the field as a starter for the Rebels again. Simmons was replaced by Trinidad Chambliss and we all know how that turned out. If the season ended today, Ole Miss would more than likely be in the college football playoff. The Rebels outgained Vanderbilt in yards last week 409-343 and forced four turnovers. The Rebels defense had its best showing against a P4 opponent holding the Commodores to 2.8 yards per carry, four punts, and two turnover on downs. The offense received a boost with Kewan Lacy returning to the lineup. Lacy ran for 39 yards and a touchdown on seven carries in the first half as Pete Golding eased him back into action. The Rebels ran for 196 yards and three scores, while Trinidad Chambliss accounted for one of those on top of airing it out for three touchdowns and 213 yards. Ole Miss looked like a contender out of the bye week, but Missouri is a step up in completion and playing well with their 1-2 punch of Simmons and Roberts. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Missouri vs Ole Miss Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Time: 3:30 PM Eastern Site: Vaught-Hemingway Stadium City: Oxford, MS TV/Streaming: SEC Network Game Odds for Ole Miss vs Missouri The latest odds as of Friday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Missouri Tigers (+185), Ole Miss Rebels (-225) Spread: Ole Miss -5.5 (-105) Total: 58.5 points #13 Missouri Tigers Head Coach: Eli Drinkwitz 2026 Record: 5-1 (2-1) Offensive Points Per Game: 35.8 (33rd) Defensive Points Per Game: 16.6 (25th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 43rd 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 2nd The Missouri Tigers Offense: Missouri ran impressive in the win over Texas A&M. The Tigers ran for 247 rushing yards and the Aggies had 216 as a team. Missouri posted 394 yards of offense and had 20 first downs to Texas A&M’s 10. Missouri scored on five out of 10 drives starting from the second quarter and Jamal Roberts had back-to-back 200-yard rushing performances. Roberts is the hottest running back in the country right now with 211 and 222 rushing yards against Florida and Texas A&M, along with five touchdowns. Roberts has four games of 100-plus yards this season and scored in five out of six games. Missouri Player to Watch on Offense: QB Austin Simmons Austin Simmons is set for a revenge game against Ole Miss and the guy who replaced him; Trinidad Chambliss . This will be fun! Simmons has looked great for Missouri and threw a season-high 340 yards against Florida two weeks ago. Simmons has four multi-touchdown games and tossed three scores against Kansas and Mississippi State. He wasn’t asked to air it out early in the season, but over the past three games he’s averaged 32.3 pass attempts per game compared to 22.6 in the first three weeks. If Jamal Roberts can’t find running lanes, then Simmons will surely be dropping back 30-plus times and looking to take matters into his own hands late. Simmons has 11 rushing attempts on the season and hasn’t scored a touchdown on the ground yet. He’s a sneaky anytime touchdown bet. The Missouri Tigers Defense: Versus a DI opponent, Missouri allowed a season-low in yards last week to Texas A&M at 216. Only 27 of those yards came on the ground as the Aggies were held to 1.2 yards per carry and no touchdowns. Missouri picked off Marcel Reed twice and held him to 19-of-39 (48.7%). Missouri ranks tied for 13th nationally with 3.0 sacks per game and ranks tied for 9th with 18 sacks on the season. The Tigers grabbed three sacks last week are they’re coming into the week at 31.2% on third downs (26th). Missouri held Texas A&M to 4-of-18 last week on third downs (22.2%). Missouri will be bringing the pressure, but Chambliss thrives under duress. It should be a fun to watch the chess match between Missouri’s edge rushers and Chambliss. Missouri Player to Watch on Defense: EDGE Deaden Hopkins Deaden Hopkins has only played in four out of Missouri’s six games, but boy has he made his presence felt. Hopkins has at least a 0.5 sack in all four games, including Texas A&M last week. Hopkins had a career-high 3.5 sacks at Mississippi State after posting 1.5 sacks versus both Troy and Kansas, plus a forced fumble and recovery in both too. If you catch yourself going “who was that” or “that was close to being offsides"; it’s probably Hopkins off the ball you’re talking about. The Rebels scored 52 at Vanderbilt and 409 yards of offense. Ole Miss ran for 196 yards and Kewan Lacy made his return in limited fashion. Three different players ran for a touchdown, including Trinidad Chambliss . The star quarterback tossed three touchdowns and 213 yards on 20-of-30 (66.6%), plus the rushing score. The Rebels average 300.6 passing yards per game (15th), but 104th in rushing yards per game (133.2). Luckily, Missouri’s weak spot is their secondary as they rank 71st in coverage grades as to the 21st rush grade on defense. Ole Miss Player to Watch on Offense: RB Kewan Lacy Kewan Lacy only had seven carries in his return following the bye week, but had an efficient 39 yards and a two-yard touchdown. Lacy broke off a 19-yarder in the first quarter and that was the only other highlight as he didn’t receive a carry in the second half. Pete Golding say he wanted to slowly bring back Lacy last week, but with a ranked matchup versus Missouri, we can expect at least double-digit touches for Lacy this weekend. The Ole Miss Rebels Defense: The Ole Miss defense forced four turnovers at Vanderbilt on two interceptions and two fumbles. The Rebels grabbed a pair of turnover in each half and held Vanderbilt to a punt, turnover, or turnover on downs on nine out of 12 drives minus a kneel down. It was the best defensive outing of the year against a P4 opponent. Ole Miss grabbed three sacks and eight TFL, plus forced three fumbles. away.headline: Injury update: Will Mario Craver play today for Texas A&M against Missouri?
away.blurb: Texas A&M star receiver Mario Craver has been listed as questionable all week against the Missouri Tigers, as he continues to recover from some bangs and bruises he has sustained throughout the season thus far. With the release of this morning's SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report , that status appears to remain for Craver with kickoff now under an hour and a half away. Craver is listed as a game-time decision for the Aggies in this report, meaning that fans will be sweating his status heading right up into the game. Craver's skill set makes him one of the toughest matchups for A&M's opponents on the entire team, so having him ready and available for the Aggies is key in this matchup. There are some positive signs for Craver going into this game, though: he was spotted heading out to warm up against the Tigers, potentially signaling that he will be ready to go. Warmups are warmups, but if he was trending towards not playing, this would not be happening. This is a similar pattern, though, to what we saw against Arkansas last week. Craver was listed as questionable throughout the week and called a game time decision against the Hogs, but he eventually was ready to go and saw a good number of snaps in the first half. He didn't play much of the later part of the game, as it looked like he had tweaked something in the touches he did get. Maybe that was out of a sense of safety, though, as the Aggies had the game well in hand by halftime, and were much more committed to the run than they were the pass against the Hogs. He eventually left the game with an apparent injury , though he did return later on in the contest. There was a similar story the following week against LSU, however: he was targeted a lot earlier on in the game, but eventually had to leave with some sort of injury before returning. Especially with Terry Bussey out, though, Craver's availability is paramount. There was a good showing from TK Norman last week, who looks ready to step into an increased role, but there's a big difference between Arkansas at home and Missouri on the road. away.headline: Ahmad Hardy injury update: Star Missouri football RB not yet back in practice
away.blurb: Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz said that there currently is no change to the Mizzou football running back’s injury status during his press availability Tuesday, Oct. 13. Drinkwitz said that Hardy has not yet started a two-week ramp-up period that he needs to see for the running back to return to the field. Drinkwitz, as recently as last Tuesday, said that he’d provide an update as soon as one was available. But rumors began to swirl on various online platforms Monday night, including PowerMizzou at 247Sports and on Reddit, that Hardy may be close to a return to practice. Drinkwitz was again asked about Hardy’s current status on Tuesday. The message board poster has become quite popular for a string of Mizzou predictions over the past year, some of which have panned out. “If he practices, I promise, I'll tweet it out. I won't even give it to Pete (ESPN reporter Pete Thamel),” Drinkwitz said. “We'll just do it ourselves. So, again, I think it's going to be really important — I know everybody's excited about where we're at and all that good stuff. When he's available, I promise you we’ll be excited to use him. But that’s not the story right now. So, nothing new.” Mizzou has its idle week after the game against the Rebels. That technically means that if Hardy is able to return to practice sometime this week, he would be in a position to possibly return for Mizzou’s next game Oct. 31 at Arkansas. home.blurb: Joseph underwent ankle surgery to address the injury, Ole Miss on SI confirmed. There isn't a timetable for his return at this point but it almost certainly rules him out for the Mizzou game. The initial SEC injury report on Wednesday evening will shed light on his official status. As it turns out, it appears that second opinion resulted in the surgery. Joseph was in Birmingham, AL on Tuesday, potentially where he spoke with doctors. Ole Miss Corner Edwin Joseph Undergoes Surgery After Injury Skip to main content SI.COM The Ole Miss Rebels are dealing with a notable injury in their secondary ahead of Saturday's SEC matchup with the Missouri Tigers in Oxford. Ole Miss defensive back Edwin Joseph suffered an ankle injury in last week's blowout win over Vanderbilt. His status remained unclear in the days after the game. But now, there's serious doubt about his availability over the next few weeks. Edwin Joseph Posts Pictures After Surgery Ole Miss safety Edwin Joseph during a fall camp practice in Oxford. | Ole Miss Athletics Joseph shared pictures on social media after surgery with two thumbs up. Joseph shared pictures on social media after surgery with two thumbs up. A transfer from Florida State, Joseph is in his first year with the Rebels, making it unfortunate to see him dealing with an injury that required midseason surgery. Through five games so far this season, Joseph has tallied 18 total tackles (11 solo) and one pass defended. The Ole Miss secondary has had its issues but Joseph has been one of the better players in the back end of Pete Golding's defense. Edwin Joseph underwent surgery for his ankle today, per his Instagram. Unlikely he plays Saturday against Missouri pic.twitter.com/I4b1k2DvJE Edwin Joseph Got Second Opinion on Ankle Injury Golding told reporters earlier this week that Joseph would be getting a second opinion on his ankle. "My only concern from Saturday, from an injury standpoint, would be Edwin," Golding said. "It is an ankle. Got diagnosed yesterday with an ankle sprain. We're going to get another opinion on that tomorrow. We'll manage it throughout the week." Missouri's offensive identity is predicated on running the football with Jamal Roberts, but the game could be decided by how the secondary fares against what feels like one of the more surprising passing games in the SEC this season. As usual, the game has ACC and national title race implications , though this season those conversations are focused far more on Miami, which finished last season as the national runner-up and is currently the heavy favorite to win the ACC in 2026. Things are far different for Florida State and embattled coach Mike Norvell, who entered the year facing serious job pressure and now risks falling to 3-4 on the season and 1-3 in ACC play if the Seminoles cannot pull a stunning upset. Wins against Miami in 2021, 2022 and 2023 were crucial building blocks of Norvell's eventual ACC Championship run, but now it's Mario Cristobal who has the chance to string together three straight wins in the series after the Hurricanes got the better of Florida State in 2024 and 2025. The return to Miami Gardens also spotlights what has become a notable home-field advantage for Miami in this recent run, as the Hurricanes are 15-1 at home since the start of the 2024 season, including that 36-14 win against the Seminoles in Hard Rock Stadium two years ago. Miami has been absolute rock stars in the ACC and the sport as a whole, continuing the momentum from the team's College Football Playoff run with eye-popping scores and stat-stuffing performances to start the 2026 season. Florida State hopes to provide more resistance than the average Miami opponent, but even that might not be enough to stop the ACC's most potent national title contender. Miami vs. Florida State: Need to know A big stage for Darian Mensah's Heisman Trophy case: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been playing at an elite level all season, but the lopsided wins and predicted blowouts haven't given him the stage and audience that Saturday night's rivalry game will command. Miami may be in a far better place than Florida State this season, but this iconic rivalry will still bring the attention of Heisman Trophy voters to Hard Rock Stadium to see how Mensah performs under the pressure. Currently, he's one of just two FBS quarterbacks with 15-plus passing touchdowns and zero interceptions and boasts the best completion percentage (84.2%) and passer rating (212.2) in all of FBS. Mensah will still have a road trip to Notre Dame and a few other opportunities to shine in the spotlight, but Saturday night could prove to be the launching point for Mensah to push Jeremiah Smith in the Heisman conversation. Florida State struggling against top teams : While Florida State has won three national championships and spent 72 weeks ranked No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll throughout its history, the Seminoles have struggled against the best teams in recent years. As the Seminoles take aim at their rival from the South, they do so staring down a brutal losing streak against top-3 teams from the AP poll. Florida State has lost its last eight games against AP top-three teams, last winning in the BCS National Championship Game against Auburn at the end of the 2013 season. Another losing streak that Florida State can put to bed on Saturday night is a 12-game road losing streak against teams with any AP ranking, which stretches back to a 2016 win at Miami. No one is beating teams like Miami is in 2026 : The Hurricanes enter this annual rivalry checkpoint with one of the most dominant teams in the country, beating opponents by an average of 39.8 points per game. That's the largest points-per-game differential through five games in school history and is currently the largest among all FBS teams. Now, a skeptic would be quick to point out that a 70-point win against Florida A&M will do a lot to juice those averages, but it's the consistency with which Miami has been blitzing its opponents that stands out. Of Miami's five games, only one (a 33-20 win at Wake Forest ) was decided by less than 28 points. Where to watch Miami vs. Florida State live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 7 p.m. ET Location : Hard Rock Stadium -- Miami Gardens, Fla. TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Miami vs. Florida State prediction, picks Miami isn't just blowing teams out on the scoreboard this season; it's a team that's also been exceeding oddsmakers' expectations nearly every week. The Hurricanes indeed have the best point differential in FBS (+39.8), but they also rank T-14 nationally with a 4-1 record against the spread and carry the 15th-best cover margin in the country, beating the spread by an average of 7.8 points per game. With those kinds of trends, it's tough to think that Miami is a candidate for an upset alert, and Florida State's road woes make it very possible that this game will get sideways on the Seminoles. Can the struggling Seminoles avoid another embarrassing defeat? One of college football's fiercest rivalries returns as No. 3 Miami (5-0) hosts Florida State (3-3) at Hard Rock Stadium. These two programs couldn't be heading in more different directions. Miami is coming off a dominant 41-13 victory over Clemson and remains firmly in the national championship conversation. Meanwhile, Florida State suffered an embarrassing 44-20 loss to Louisville after blowing an early 14-0 lead. With Miami entering as a heavy favorite, Mike Norvell and the Seminoles could be in serious trouble. Miami: The Hurricanes Look UNSTOPPABLE Mario Cristobal has built one of the most complete teams in college football, and quarterback Darian Mensah is playing like a legitimate Heisman Trophy contender. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards, 15 touchdowns, and zero interceptions this season. Miami is averaging an incredible 49.6 points per game while allowing just 9.8. Freshman sensation Malachi Toney has been nearly impossible to defend, recording 604 receiving yards and six touchdowns. His explosiveness gives Miami a dangerous weapon against a Florida State secondary that has struggled against quality competition. Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. provides another dimension to the offense, and Miami should have opportunities to establish the run against a vulnerable Seminoles defense. Florida State: Mike Norvell Is Running Out of Answers Florida State's season has quickly become a disappointment. The Seminoles allowed an unbelievable 397 rushing yards against Louisville, including 235 yards from Isaac Brown. That's a massive problem against Miami's balanced offense. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has thrown for 1,320 yards, eight touchdowns, and seven interceptions this season. Although Daniels has been dangerous with his legs, his inconsistency as a passer could become a serious issue against Miami's defense. Running back Ousmane Kromah has been productive with 565 rushing yards, but the Seminoles cannot rely entirely on their ground game if Miami builds an early lead. Florida State has enough athleticism to make some plays, but its defensive struggles and offensive turnovers make this an extremely difficult matchup. How Each Team Wins For Miami, the formula is simple: establish the run, protect the football, and allow Mensah to attack Florida State's secondary. Defensively, the Hurricanes must contain Daniels' rushing ability and force him to win from the pocket. For Florida State, everything starts with controlling possession. The Seminoles must establish Kromah, limit Miami's explosive plays, and create turnovers. If Florida State allows this game to become a shootout, it could get ugly quickly. I simply don't see Florida State having enough answers for Miami's offense. Mensah has been outstanding, and I expect him to continue his Heisman-caliber season against a Seminoles defense that just surrendered 44 points to Louisville. Florida State should create a few explosive plays with Daniels and Kromah, especially early, but Miami's defense will eventually take control. I expect the Hurricanes to establish a comfortable halftime lead before completely taking over in the second half. Final Score: No. 3 Miami 45, Florida State 20 Miami remains undefeated, improves to 6-0, and strengthens its national championship case. And yes, even in 2026, these to bring something special when they play. This isn't one of those rivalries that defy logic and reason, like Oklahoma beating Texas last week in a Red River Rivalry that gets totally funky. But there are always interesting storylines surrounding these two. Miami is trying to keep a dominant 2026 going with Notre Dame coming up in a few weeks, and Florida State is looking for another stunning performance like the 38-7 win over Virginia a few weeks ago. It's Florida State vs Miami. Something interesting will happen. Florida State vs Miami: Quick Hits Miami gets Pitt home next before two massive road games at North Carolina and then the big one – Notre Dame. Florida State goes on the road for three games in the next four, with a week off before hosting Clemson. Miami was pushed in a 28-22 win last year and has won six of the last nine since losing 20-19 in 2016. How To Watch Florida State vs Miami Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 7:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens, FL – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Florida State Will Win Florida State wins when it runs well. The Seminoles also win when they score points and keep the other team from scoring points – duh, that's how it's supposed to work. The offense is great when it finds its groove on the ground – going 3-0 when coming up with more than 4.4 yards per carry – and that helps when the defense is doing its job, so the FSU passing game doesn't have to press. That won't be easy, but if the Seminoles can pop a few early runs, that takes the pressure off everything else. Why Miami Will Win Florida State probably won't get the ground game rolling like it needs to against the No. 1 run defense in college football. The Noles were able to rumble from the start against Virginia, but they struggled against SMU, and they weren't close to getting going in the losses to Alabama and Louisville. Clemson can run at times, and so can Wake Forest, and they didn't go anywhere. Miami has allowed 213 rushing yards on the year, giving up fewer than two yards per carry. Florida State vs Miami Prediction, Betting Lines Miami won't get caught up in the emotion. It'll step up the defense after the first ten minutes, and then Darian Mensah will go to work. The Miami star is hitting 84% of his passes, and he's not going to force anything. It'll be a cold, mechanical performance by the Hurricanes without any real drama after starting to pull away in the third quarter. picks.blurb: Miami vs. Florida State Preview: No. 3 Hurricanes Prepare for Rivalry Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Miami vs. Florida State Preview: No. 3 Hurricanes Prepare for Rivalry Showdown Photo by: Ashley Tumlin Stephan Stroud Wed, October 14, 2026 at 8:12 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Miami Hurricanes and Florida State Seminoles will renew their rivalry Saturday night when No. 3 Miami hosts Florida State at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens. Miami enters the matchup undefeated at 5-0 overall and 3-0 in ACC play, while Florida State sits at 3-3 and 1-2 in conference action. The Hurricanes are coming off a bye week, while the Seminoles are looking to rebound from a 44-20 loss to Louisville. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. With Miami chasing a potential College Football Playoff appearance and Florida State searching for consistency, this rivalry game carries plenty of importance. Darian Mensah Leads Miami's Offense Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been outstanding during the Hurricanes' undefeated start. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards and 15 touchdowns without an interception, giving head coach Mario Cristobal a highly efficient passing attack. His accuracy and ability to get the ball to Miami's playmakers have helped the Hurricanes become one of the nation's most productive offenses. Wide receiver Malachi Toney has emerged as a major weapon, while Miami's running game gives the offense another way to control games. Running backs Mark Fletcher Jr. and Javian Mallory have combined for 596 rushing yards, helping Miami maintain a balanced attack. Cristobal's team has also been strong defensively, allowing fewer than 10 points per game in ACC competition. That balance has helped Miami establish itself as a serious contender for the conference title. Florida State Needs a Response Florida State enters the rivalry looking for answers after its disappointing loss at Louisville. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has been one of the Seminoles' most dangerous rushing threats, scoring 10 rushing touchdowns through six games. Running back Ousmane Kromah has also been productive, recording 565 rushing yards. Head coach Mike Norvell will need his offense to maintain that rushing production while limiting mistakes against Miami's defense. The Seminoles have shown they can compete with strong opponents, including an early season lead against Alabama, but they have struggled to finish games consistently. Defensively, Florida State must improve its run defense after allowing 397 rushing yards against Louisville. That weakness could be especially concerning against Miami's powerful backfield. A Rivalry With Major Stakes Miami has won the last two meetings between the programs and will look to extend that streak at home. The Hurricanes want to remain undefeated and strengthen their national championship hopes. Florida State needs a complete performance to get its season back on track. With Mensah leading Miami and Daniels providing a dual-threat presence for Florida State, the quarterback matchup will be a key storyline. Saturday night offers Miami another opportunity to make a statement, while Florida State faces a difficult test against its biggest rival.

picks.headline: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Miami (FL)
picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Miami (FL) | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation October 17, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football FSU looks to avoid 14th straight loss in games away from Doak The Florida State Seminoles (3-3, 1-2) are in North Dade for their annual rivalry game against the 3rd-ranked Miami (FL) Hurricanes at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m., and ESPN will televise the game. Miami (5-0, 3-0) leads the all-time series 37-33, while FSU holds a 21-19 edge in games played at Miami. The Seminoles are 13-9 in the series since Miami joined the ACC before the 2004 season but have lost the last two games, including a 28-22 loss last season in Tallahassee. FSU’s last victory over UM came in 2023, a 27-20 win at Doak, marking the Noles third win in a row against Miami (FL). UM’s Mario Cristobal is in his 5th season and has a 40-19 record in Miami and a 102-79 overall career record as a head coach. Miami opened its 2026 ACC slate with three straight road game wins over Stanford, Wake Forest, and Clemson and is one of only three teams with three Power-4 road wins. Miami is coming off a bye week after a 41-13 win over Clemson on the road last time out on Oct. 3. UM, led by mercenary QB Darian Mensah, who was purchased away from Duke via the transfer portal, has thrown 15 touchdowns with no interceptions. Mark Fletcher Jr. is their rushing leader, averaging 76.75 yards per game with 5 touchdowns, followed by freshman Javian Mallory, who averages 57.8 yards per game and has scored 3 TD’s. Receiver Malachi Toney, a name Seminole fans will get tired of hearing, is Mensah’s favorite target, catching 39 passes with a 15.49 average and 6 touchdowns. Cooper Barkate, who was part of the Mensah portal purchase package from Duke, is 2nd on the team with 19 receptions with a 12.68 average per game and 4 touchdowns. Overall, 14 players have caught passes from UM quarterbacks this season, 21 different players have gained 10-or-more scrimmage yards, and 11 different players have 100+ scrimmage yards this year. Miami’s defense is ranked 1st in points allowed (9.8), 1st against the run (42.6), 5th in total defense (249.6), 69th against the pass, T-25th in red zone defense, and 8th in sacks per game. Former FSU kicker Jake Weinberg is perfect in his 5 field goal attempts. Florida State will try to avoid its 14th straight loss in games away from Doak after coming off an embarrassing performance at Louisville, when after jumping out to a 14-0 lead, the Cardinals outscored FSU 44-6 the rest of the way to their 44-20 win. Louisville 44, FSU 20: Seminoles blow early lead in latest embarrassing loss Florida State’s offense is ranked 56th in the nation in total offense, 62nd in scoring, 43rd in rushing, 80th in passing, and 73rd in red-zone offense. After giving up three touchdown runs of 40-plus yards (97, 44, 68) and allowing Louisville to rack up 537 total yards, FSU’s defense now ranks 122nd in the nation, giving up 410 yards/game, 114th in passing defense (244 yards/game), 100th in third-down percentage allowing opponents to convert 41% of the time on third-down attempts, and T-120th in first-down defense allowing their opponents 129 first downs this season. Florida State is currently trending as a 21.5-point underdog, with the over/under set at 56.5 points, according to FanDuel. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Miami Hurricanes Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Jordan Silversmith (season record: 5-1) Not sure how much needs to be written here. The Hurricanes have a positional advantage at every spot, better coordinators than FSU, and are coming off a bye while playing at home. If being a 21-point underdog doesn’t explain the differences between the two teams, nothing will. We can talk about why there’s such a difference another day, but for Saturday, UM wins and covers. UM 45, FSU 17 Jessi Wynn (season record: 3-1) Although we’ve really seen Ashton Daniels come into his own and emerge as a leader on offense, I’m not sure it’ll be enough to take down the undefeated 5-0 Hurricanes. FSU showed a ton of potential during its two-game winning streak, but last week’s tough loss to Louisville was a setback. With Miami playing as well as it has, I just don’t think I can put my neck on the line for the Seminoles this week. Miami 35 , Noles 24 NoleThruandThru (season record: 6-0) I’m just here so I don’t get fined, especially this week. Like Ludacris says, Mario fills cups like Double Ds. Miami 62, FSU 20 Jon Marchant (season record: 5-1 ) The Hurricanes certainly look like a national title contender, though we may not know for certain until the playoffs. Miami might face only one top 25 team this regular season, and it’s not Florida State. Miami is much more talented, and whatever issues Mario Cristobal may or may not still have regarding game management it’s likely equalized by Mike Norvell’s own problems in that area. Is this Norvell’s last game? We’ll have to see. If he’s still the coach next Saturday I think the decision to retain him is being made after an embarrassing loss to a rival. Miami 52 , FSU 16 Tim Scribble (season record: 5-1) Miami should be able to name their score in this one. I expect Mario and crew to embarrass Florida State. Miami 50+, FSU 17 Matt Minnick (Season record: 4-2; ATS: 4-2) I felt so good about my pick to win last week after the first quarter. Wow, what an unmitigated disaster. Once again Mike Norvell’s program shows it is unable to take a punch, pick itself off the mat, and punch back. Strange things can happen in rivalry games right? Just look at OU shocking Texas last week in the Red River Rivalry. Maybe FSU can pull off a similar stu—haha, who am I kidding? I can’t even type the sentence without smirking. FSU’s secondary couldn’t cover a twin mattress with a king sheet. Now it must stop Mensah, Toney, and company? Come on. Mario Cristobal can smell blood in the water and he’s primed to attack. Miami leads by 20+ at the half and cruises. Miami 48, FSU 14 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-2 ) FSU is so cooked. That is all that needs to be said. Darian Mensah is playing like a Heisman-level quarterback. He hasn’t thrown a single interception this year. Everything about Miami says absurd in terms of their quality of play. Now, they haven’t played *anyone* worth being No. 3, but they have convincingly won against bad teams. Doesn’t matter. FSU is getting clobbered. Miami 67, FSU 3 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 4-1) Mario’s propensity to blow one isn’t going to stop this bloodbath. Miami 52 , FSU 17 Frank DNole (season record: 3-3) I am a broken FSU fan. However, while SCum is heavily favored, this game is actually a win-win for FSU. If FSU wins by playing its best road game since November 25, 2023, as 21-point dogs, at the rented stadium, against one of the top teams in the country in terms of buying transfer players in hopes of becoming relevant again after 25 years of mediocrity under 5 different head coaches, each of whom proclaimed they would bring back the u (Coker, Shannon, Golden, Richt, Diaz, and Cristoball), that would be cool. If that were to happen, it would be the biggest humiliation the Noles could give scum since the 47-0 thrashing in 1997 and could possibly cost them heavily in the polls and later in possible playoff consideration. #winning If FSU loses, especially if blown out, the Noles still win, in that it will speed up what needs to be done to move FSU along on making the needed changes on Sunday morning. SCum thinks they will be putting the final nail in Norvell’s tenure, and while that may be true, they are doing the Noles a favor by possibly forcing the administration to act sooner than they may have wanted to. If that happens and the delusional scummers think it happened because they beat FSU, bless their hearts, all it will do is help speed up what was going to happen anyway and what most Noles want. So thanks? #winning Here is how I’m going to look at this game: Florida State is the last program to win a national championship in the state of Florida. FSU has won 5 ACC titles since scum joined the self-proclaimed All Canes Conference in 2004, and they still have zero titles 21 years later. Kudos to them for buying their way into the playoffs last year, but until you win an ACC title or a National Championship, a win tonight would just be another meaningless regular-season win. If scum, with the amount of money they have invested in their star-studded roster, do not win the National Championship, or at the very least the ACC championship this year, they never will. Finally, as a broken Seminole fan, I will watch this game with zero expectations, comfortably numb (shout to TN member ?), with the TV on mute and listening to Rage Against The Machine being played backwards. That said, FSU players… blah blah 110% more effort, blah… want it more, and blah blah… more heart than their more talented and better coached opponent. FSU Seminoles 37, FMFFM 34 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 3-3, 3-3 ATS) In 2024, we saw Mario Cristobal play it relatively safe instead of attempting to set a new record for margin of victory (47) in the series, with Miami winning by “just” 22. I don’t think that happens this year, a season where the Hurricanes are trying to make up for their lack of a difficult schedule with blowouts on top of trying to pad stats for Darian Mensah’s finish-in-second Heisman campaign. Florida State won’t be shut out, Ousmane Kromah should have at least a few exciting runs and maybe another cool Micahi Danzy catch. Outside of that, though, barring a hilarious meltdown from Miami, that should be just about the extent of positive takeaways from the matchup. picks.headline: 7 bold predictions for Miami's rivalry matchup against the Florida State Seminoles
picks.blurb: 7 bold predictions for Miami's rivalry matchup against the Florida State Seminoles Skip to main content About Canes Football Canes Basketball FanSided NCAA Sites Hurricanes All-Time Football Lists Canes Football Recruiting Hurricanes All-Time Basketball Lists Miami Hurricanes Basketball Recruiting The Joe Gaither Show on CanesCentral Saturday's game at Hard Rock Stadium between the Miami Hurricanes and Florida State Seminoles will show two programs at opposite ends of the development process. Mario Cristobal has Miami sitting at 5-0 after a run to the CFP national championship game, and Mike Norvell is once again fighting for his job after a 3-3 start for Florida State. Here are seven bold predictions for the matchup. 1. Ashton Daniels finishes with fewer than 30 rushing yards Daniels enters Saturday with 323 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns, so holding him under 30 looks aggressive on the surface. But roughly 42% of those yards, and half of the touchdowns, came in one game, when he ran for 136 yards and five scores against Virginia. Alabama held him to seven net rushing yards on 13 attempts, and Louisville limited him to 45 yards on 13 attempts last week. Miami has also had some success against mobile quarterbacks this year. Wake Forest's Gio Lopez had rushed for 97 yards in his first two games before finishing with minus-8 yards against the Hurricanes (only 11 yards once three sacks are removed). Clemson's Tait Reynolds had 92 rushing yards in his previous three games before finishing at minus-22. Miami has allowed zero quarterback rushing touchdowns this season. The under-30 yards prediction can also be paired with Daniels not scoring a rushing touchdown. The Hurricanes have allowed only one rushing touchdown all year, from Clemson running back Gideon Davidson in the fourth quarter, and zero in the first half. 2. Florida State finishes below 100 rushing yards as a team Florida State has 1,123 rushing yards on the season and averages 187.2 per game, fourth in the ACC, so holding the Seminoles under 100 would be huge for the Hurricanes. But Miami has surrendered only 14 rushing first downs all season, so there is some merit to this one. Florida State averages 4.84 yards per rush overall but falls to 3.02 when the score is tied, 3.46 when trailing by 8-14 points and 2.11 when trailing by 15 or more. Its largest rushing totals have come disproportionately while playing from ahead. Miami's opponents have averaged 1.07 yards per carry in the second quarter and 0.86 in the third. On second downs the Hurricanes have allowed 10 yards on 33 rushing attempts, or 0.30 per carry. If Miami gets ahead, Florida State's best offensive weapon will fade. 3. Miami rushes for at least 250 yards Miami already averages 220.4 rushing yards and 6.16 yards per carry, ranking third in the ACC in rushing yardage. Florida State is 14th in the ACC in rushing defense, allowing 993 yards so far this season (4.60 per carry through six games). In matchups against FBS opponents, the Seminoles are allowing 6.67 yards per rush with a 50% rushing success rate. Louisville ran for 397 yards and six touchdowns on 43 carries last week, averaging 9.2 yards per attempt, with Isaac Brown accounting for 235 yards. Miami would not need anything close to that efficiency to reach 250. At its current 6.16 yards per carry, 41 rushing attempts would produce roughly 253 yards. A game in which Miami is favored by three touchdowns creates a second-half script that could push the Hurricanes past 40 attempts. 4. Miami sacks Ashton Daniels at least five times Florida State has allowed 16 sacks through six games, third-most in the ACC behind only Virginia (2.67 per game). Miami has generated 16 sacks in five games, with the totals rising from one against Stanford to two against Florida A&M, three against Wake Forest, four against Central Michigan and six against Clemson. The prediction should come true if Miami stops the run and forces Florida State into obvious passing situations. Daniels is completing 59.5% of his passes with eight touchdowns and seven interceptions, and he drops to 53.6% in second halves. When Florida State is trailing by 8-14 points, its team completion percentage falls to 37.5%. Five sacks is a large number, but Miami just recorded six against another mobile quarterback in Reynolds while Florida State ranks among the ACC leaders in sacks allowed. 5. Darian Mensah completes at least 80% of his passes An 80% completion prediction against Florida State sounds high, but Mensah is completing 84.2% of his passes for the season. He has finished at 85% or better in four of five games, with Clemson's 66.7% the only exception. His first-half passing numbers are 80-of-92, and he is 37-of-40 in first quarters. Florida State has been particularly vulnerable early through the air, with opponents completing 76.1% of first-quarter passes. Overall the Seminoles have allowed nine passing touchdowns against three interceptions and FBS opponents have averaged roughly 7.3 yards per dropback against Florida State. 6. Florida State does not score a rushing touchdown Florida State has 16 rushing touchdowns, 10 from Daniels, and 15 of them have come in the red zone. Miami has allowed one rushing touchdown on 116 carries, and inside the red zone, opponents have rushed 12 times for 14 yards (1.17 per carry) with one touchdown. Teams have reached Miami's red zone only eight times in five games. This one has potential to be spoiled in garbage time, but this is about being bold and Miami's run defense has been stout. 7. Miami wins by at least 28 points Miami is favored by 21.5 points, and their average victory margin is 39.8 points, the best in the country and the largest through five games in program history. Only Wake Forest has finished within 28 points. Last week the Seminoles led Louisville 14-0 before being outscored 44-6 the rest of the way. If Miami can do everything already mentioned, a final margin in the range of 49-10 makes sense. away.headline: Initial week 7 injury report for Florida State vs. No. 3 Miami could spell disaster for the Seminoles
away.blurb: Florida State needs some luck on its side to take down Miami, but that might not happen with multiple players notably absent from the initial injury report . The Hurricanes had two starters in particular suffer injuries last time out against Clemson, but neither player was included in the injury report, which means the Seminoles will be getting the best version of Miami in Week 7. DB Romanas Frederique Jr. (out) LB Noah LaVallee (questionable) No Lightfoot and no McCoy on the injury report likely means Florida State will be playing against a full-strength Miami team. The Hurricanes have a few players who have been ruled out for the game, but nothing serious has changed from last week. That could be an issue for the Seminoles, who already will face two serious mismatches in Week 7. The Hurricanes' offense could also receive a boost if McCoy avoids having to sit out the Week 7 game against the Seminoles. There is no two ways about it, Florida State has struggled to generate consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks this season. The performance against Virginia in Week 5 was exceptional, but it should be viewed as the outlier at this point, with more disappointing performances than positive ones on defense. Florida State is just days away from perhaps the biggest game on the schedule against ACC rivals No. 3 Miami. The Hurricanes have displayed arguably the best offense and the best defense in the country this season, while the Seminoles have struggled to play consistent football. Starting edge rusher and Miami's sack leader, Marquise Lightfoot, left the game against Clemson early, but the star defender was not included in the first Week 7 injury report. Additionally, starting right tackle Matthew McCoy was attended to by the training staff against the Tigers, but ultimately played the rest of the game. McCoy was also not included in the initial Week 7 injury report for Miami. LSU might have the best mix of talent, and it certainly has the highest-profile head coach, but it has two losses, and one of them was last week in a 35-34 overtime thriller to Kentucky. It's just assumed that Texas will find its way into the College Football Playoff, and maybe get to the SEC Championship first. But it just lost to an Oklahoma team that pulled off an all-time found-a-way 27-24 win in the Red River Rivalry. The Sooners only have one SEC loss – 41-13 to Georgia – but all of a sudden, the second half of the schedule doesn't seem that bad. Kentucky, because it's in the first year of the Will Stein era, and Oklahoma, because it beat Texas – both programs are in a good place. But the winner of this will still be alive in the SEC, and the other almost certainly won't. Kentucky vs Oklahoma: Quick Hits Oklahoma goes on the road for two of the next three weeks, traveling to Mississippi State, hosting South Carolina, and going to Florida. It's a key stretch for Kentucky with Vanderbilt at home next, followed by a date at Tennessee. The two programs have only met three times. Oklahoma won 29-8 in 1982 and 29-7 in 1980, but Bear Bryant's Kentucky won the 1951 Sugar Bowl. No turnovers on the road at Texas A&M and South Carolina, and none last week against LSU. And then there are the penalties – there aren't any. Kentucky is No. 1 in the SEC in fewest penalties and fewest penalty yards, and that matters. The lack of turnovers matters. It all matters, because Oklahoma probably can't pull this off without the Wildcats royally screwing up like Texas did last week. Why Oklahoma Will Win Kentucky needs its running game to rock, and that's going to be a problem. Georgia was able to power away on Oklahoma with a few big runs in the blowout win, but that's been about it. Michigan tried to run a lot, and it did just enough to get by, but it was a struggle. Texas wasn't exactly creative in the way it tried to run, and it got stuffed way too often. The Sooners are 3-0 when they don't allow a touchdown run, and 0-2 when they do. Oklahoma will hold up defensively in a low-scoring game that comes down to a few key late stops, but this won't be easy for a team that failed to hit 300 yards of total offense against anyone but UTEP. Kentucky is 135th in the nation in third down conversions. Oklahoma is third in the nation in third down stops. And that's the ball game. Oklahoma defensive tackle David Stone celebrates after making a play against Kent State. | Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman Fri, October 16, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky isn't particularly great at anything (except maybe 2-point conversions), and they're not really very bad at anything. One area that is concerning is third down conversions - on both offense and defense. UK ranks 135th nationally in third down offense, and is 128th in third down defense. Give the edge to Oklahoma in that important metric, and expect to see more improvement from the OU offensive line, the OU running backs and the OU quarterback. One area Kentucky does do pretty well is turnover margin - the Wildcats rank No. 9 nationally at plus-1.17 per game. Therefore John Mateer and the Sooners might have to replicate last week's zero-turnover performance in the Cotton Bowl if they're going to extend their winning streak to two games. Final: Oklahoma 28, Kentucky 24 Oklahoma got the win it needed, but it will have to handle success to notch another victory Saturday night. Brent Venables' defense will frustrate the Kentucky offense - and potentially hand the OU offense some premium field position if Will Stein opts to roll the dice on fourth down - but this will come down to the Sooner offense. Ben Arbuckle's group needs to show that the ground game they found in the third quarter can translate week to week. If that is the case, and Oklahoma wins the turnover battle, a rejuvenated Tate Sandell could be the difference on Owen Field. Final: Oklahoma 24, Kentucky 20 OU's defense put together its best performance of 2026 last week against Texas. The unit will be put to the test when it faces off against Kentucky's high-flying offense. The Wildcats have three running backs who have rushed for over 100 yards, and Kenny Minchey has excelled at avoiding turnovers. Big plays will happen against OU's defense, like they did against Texas. But the unit is strong enough to keep the game low-scoring. That means it will be up to the offense to avoid turnovers, sustain drives and, obviously, score points. The Sooners struggled offensively against Texas. But there were a handful of positives, including Lloyd Avant's 72-yard day, John Mateer's back-to-back sideline throws to Isaiah Sategna in the fourth quarter and the offensive line's incremental improvement. If the unit can build on those positives, OU will win its second game in a row over a quality opponent. Final: Oklahoma 20, Kentucky 17 The running game wasn't even good, really, in the second half of the Red River Rivalry win. It was, however, passable as a Division I running game, which is a significant upgrade to what it looked like in the three-and-a-half games that preceded it. Oklahoma comes out and builds on that performance - not with a major jump but at least picking up an occasional first down on the ground against a defense that gave up 232 rushing yards two weeks ago against South Carolina - and is able to squeak out a win over the Wildcats. John Mateer's numbers won't be great, but he is at least able to avoid the disastrous moments that cost the Sooners against Michigan and Georgia in particular, while Oklahoma's defense continues to show that they remain one of the best in the country. Final: Oklahoma 24, Kentucky 21 Brady Trantham Both teams are coming off emotional wins. While Kentucky has disadvantages in this game, they are a more complete team - albeit with a lower ceiling - than inconsistentOklahoma. It is difficult to see the offense either becoming something more against a far worse defense than they've faced over the last month or keeping pace with Stein's attack in the event the defense lets up a few scores. Kentucky is an old, experienced team. They've not played much football together, but going on the road in an environment like Oklahoma isn't going to shock them. OU rallies late but can't dig out of the hole it dug for itself with first-half turnovers. picks.headline: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling
picks.blurb: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Story by Wildcats Wire Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 4:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels down to Norman to face the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, and both of these teams have plenty of momentum coming into this matchup. Arguably no team in the country has more momentum on their side than the Wildcats right now, coming off back-to-back walk off two-point conversions for the win in overtime. However, Oklahoma came off of their bye week and got a massive win over Texas in the Red River Rivalry game. With that being said, do not let the final score fool you, Oklahoma is still really struggling on offense. Oklahoma's offense will be the worst unit on the field this Saturday, and despite a big 27-24 win over Texas, the issues have not been fixed. The Sooners have scored just six offensive touchdowns since week two. They have only scored over 20 points twice this season, this was week one against UTEP and against Texas where they needed a blocked punt for a touchdown and a pick six to do so. This is a night game in Norman and will present a lot of adversity for Kentucky. The matchup to watch is the Kentucky offense versus the Oklahoma defense, but we will get into that side later. Basically every single offensive metric that you look at to determine offensive success, the Sooners rank bottom five in the SEC. Oklahoma ranks dead last in the conference in all of these statistics: Success rate, Rush SR%, EPA per rush, Explosive play rate and 1D+TD%. They also rank bottom five in the SEC in these statistics: EPA per play, EPA per dropback, Pass SR%, 3rd Down conversion rate, Early Down conversion rate and yards per play. This might be the worst offense Kentucky faces this season unless they can turn things around quickly. Oklahoma ranks first in the SEC in three-and-out rate and negative play percentage. The Sooners have the worst yards per carry average in the FBS. This is a stark contrast because Kentucky's defense ranks top five in the SEC in explosive % allowed and negative % forced. Kentucky's defense has excelled at three things this season: forcing turnovers, forcing negative plays and limiting explosives. This Oklahoma offense has struggled, but they do have some playmakers. The number one guy that should scare you, ironically, is number one Isaiah Sategna. Sategna is a dynamic receiver who is the one guy that can consistently create separation and he is dangerous with the football in his hands. Kentucky has to know where Sategna is on every snap because he is lightning in a bottle when he gets his hands on the football. John Mateer is a reckless but talented quarterback, he made the best throw of his season against Texas to set up the Sooners for the game winning field goal. Mateer threw a perfect back shoulder to Sategna from the far hash. Mateer has arm talent and is a dangerous runner, he immediately looks to run when a pass play breaks down. However, Mateer is extremely turnover prone, even moreso than LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt. Kentucky forced two turnovers on Leavitt, and they need to repeat that on Saturday. They have done a great job of forcing turnovers all season, they did it against Keelon Russell, Marcel Reed, LaNorris Sellers and Leavitt. This defensive line has to get pressure on Mateer to force him to play recklessly. The Wildcats have struggled with scrambling quarterbacks this season, but they were better last week against Leavitt--same thing applies this week with Mateer. Oklahoma as we stated, averages the fewest yards per carry in all of FBS. This is a game where Kentucky should be able to make Oklahoma one dimensional, which is a massive advantage for the Wildcats. The defense has to make Mateer uncomfortable in the pocket and they will have a great chance to win this football game. Kentucky's defense has the opportunity to have their best performance of the season this Saturday. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 17, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Following an emotional win vs. No. 10 LSU, Kentucky heads to Oklahoma to face a Sooners team that just beat No. 1 Texas. What a wild Saturday it was for the Kentucky Football team. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky’s offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners’ other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners’ stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer’s primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. away.blurb: Fasusi has missed each of Oklahoma's last four games after playing in a limited role in the season opener against the UTEP Miners. Head coach Brent Venables said he was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Along with Fasusi, offensive linemen Eddy Pierre-Louis and Heath Ozaeta were also listed as questionable. Both players started games for the Sooners this season. Ozaeta played against Texas despite limping off the field during warm-ups. Pierre-Louis missed the Texas game and was on crutches during the pre-game coin toss and on the sideline. Wide receiver Parker Livingstone is the only other questionable name on the injury report. Livingstone started against Texas and played 29 snaps, but didn't register a target in the game. He hasn't really produced much since coming over from Texas in the transfer portal. Livingstone has six receptions for 51 yards this season. If Fasusi, Pierre-Louis, and Ozaeta all miss the Kentucky game, the Sooners will need a new right-guard starter, likely Peyton Joseph. Cornerback Eli Bowen is a key name to watch for the Sooners' defense. He was injured in practice on Thursday and missed the win over Texas. If he doesn't play Saturday night, Trystan Haynes would get his second consecutive start after playing well against the Longhorns . For the Kentucky Wildcats, one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry).
