picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , following us on Twitter/X , and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. Published Oct 14, 2026 ADAM CARRIKER Adam’s dream of playing for the Huskers came to fruition. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! This is the season for an Oregon team that should be in full rock-and-roll mode at this point, but instead it's been one big, sad trombone of a season. The Ducks are still 3-2 with a not-that-horrible schedule the rest of the way outside of a trip to Ohio State. They lost to UCLA, but they can stay alive in the Big Ten title hunt with one more loss, even if an at-large CFP bid is likely gone with a third defeat and no Big Ten Championship. And they have to do it with Nebraska's former star quarterback, Dylan Raiola – maybe. Nebraska had Indiana cooked, but it turned the stove off too early. The Hoosiers rallied back for a 20-17 win, but that might have been more about the defending national champs not being as good this year than the Huskers being close to fantastic. However, winning in Eugene is still hard, and if Nebraska can do it, it's 6-1 with a favorable schedule – Ohio State comes to Lincoln – and all of a sudden, it's on the fast track to 10-2 – at least – and a possible at-large CFP bid. Nebraska starts a run of three road games in four dates, getting a week off before playing Washington, and then it's off to Illinois. The two have never played as Big Ten teams. Oregon won the last meeting 42-35 in 2017. The Huskers are 6-2 overall in the series, with the first win in 1952. Star quarterback Dante Moore is expected to miss another game after suffering a concussion against USC. Dylan Raiola might get his shot against his former team, but he was beyond awful against UCLA. Brock Thomas doesn't have Raiola's talent, but he got the offense moving in the second half. Nebraska gave up two huge touchdowns against Indiana, but held firm the rest of the way. Oregon's offensive problems won't all of a sudden be fixed this week. The Huskers can force takeaways – three against Michigan State, two against Maryland – but the Ducks are capable of getting their running game moving a bit to take the pressure off the passing game. The Cornhuskers are coming off a highly competitive effort in a loss to defending national champions Indiana, while the Ducks have a quarterback battle to work out with Dante Moore still sidelined as he recovers from a concussion. Here is a preview: Oregon (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) vs. Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) When: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 8 p.m. PT Where: Autzen Stadium Latest line: Oregon by 7 Radio: Oregon Sports Network Stream : You can watch this game live with Fubo (free trial), or with DIRECTV (free trial). LOOKING FOR REVENGE? Dylan Raiola will have to earn the opportunity to face his former team in Nebraska. A two-year starter for the Cornhuskers, Raiola has faced external criticism for his decision to transfer to Oregon, but he maintains a strong relationship with Nebraska coach Matt Rhule and several of his former teammates. Raiola's performance against UCLA last week was one of the worst by an Oregon quarterback in recent memory: 6 of 19 passing, 43 yards and two interceptions. This, just two weeks after a highly effective outing in relief of the injured Moore against USC. Raiola was pulled in the fourth quarter against UCLA in favor of Brock Thomas, who almost led a Ducks comeback. Akili Smith Jr. was apparently part of the quarterback competition this week, too. While it is far from a guarantee that Raiola will lead the Oregon offense out onto the field against Nebraska, his personal motivation could be enough to sharpen his focus and help earn him the chance — and perhaps bounce back in a big way performance-wise to lead the Ducks to victory. GETTING A PUSH Whether Raiola or any of the Oregon quarterbacks succeeds depends heavily on the men up front. Oregon's offensive line was dreadful last week after getting a strong push to establish the run just two weeks prior against USC. If the Ducks can't find balance and give Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill a chance to break off big plays, it will be a long day for whoever is tossing the pigskin for the Ducks and staring down Nebraska's edge rushers. Especially with top Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart listed as doubtful as of Thursday evening. Dan Lanning admitted this week that Oregon is still working out who its best five offensive linemen are. For a program that came into the season with major questions at the position and an entire spring and fall camp to figure those things out, that is a very bad sign. A MOBILE THREAT Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea is a talented athlete who can make things happen with his legs. He will provide the biggest test yet for Oregon's front seven in containing a mobile quarterback, one they failed when facing Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker but largely passed against USC's Jayden Maiava. For all the bad that showed up in Oregon's befuddling, 17-15 loss to UCLA last week, the defense played well for the most part. Save for a deep pass on the first play of the game and Wayne Knight's touchdown run in the second quarter, the Ducks looked like the defensive line unit many expected them to be coming into the season. This Saturday, maintaining that level of play will start and end with keeping Colandrea in check. Forcing him into tough situations and not allowing him to improvise into big plays on the ground could be the difference. home.blurb: What Oregon football's Dan Lanning said on Dante Moore's potential return for Nebraska game NBA Eastern Atlantic Boston Celtics Ahead of the Oregon football team taking on Nebraska, head coach Dan Lanning gives an update on a potential Dante Moore return. Add ClutchPoints on Google Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images With the Oregon football team taking on the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Saturday , the fanbase is wondering what the quarterback situation will look like and if Dante Moore is able to come back. As there would be an Oregon football quarterback competition if Moore can't go , head coach Dan Lanning 's recent comments on Moore leave the door open for a return, though it isn't set in stone. “Dan Lanning says that he's going to let the Big Ten Availability Report tell us whether or not Dante Moore would be available this week,” Neel wrote on X, formerly Twitter. “Said he's been out there practicing this week and looks great, which he's been excited to see.” MLB National East Atlanta Braves NHL Eastern Metropolitan Carolina Hurricanes According to Zachary Neel at USA Today, Lanning would say that the upcoming Big Ten Availability Report will reveal Moore's status for Saturday's contest against the Cornhuskers. However, Lanning would say that Moore “looks great” i n practice after sustaining a concussion in Sept. 26's win over the USC Trojans. More on the quarterback situation with Oregon football If Moore were to play, it would be a major boost for the Ducks in getting back one of the better quarterbacks in the country, as the other options are Raiola and Brock Thomas. In Oregon football's loss to UCLA last Saturday, Raiola threw for 43 yards and two interceptions, as he was benched for Thomas, who recorded 156 yards and a touchdown, leading to Lanning saying Monday that it will be an open competition if Moore can't make it. “This game — of course, it's going to be an emotional game for Dylan, being the place he came from. He's going to do everything he can to make sure our team is in the best situation to have success this week and be prepared. … I know he'll do that because he's a pro,” Lanning said Monday, per Pete Nakos. At any rate, it remains to be seen what Moore's status looks like for the clash against Nebraska. home.headline: What we're hearing on Oregon injuries ahead of Nebraska
home.blurb: However, it doesn't appear that things are going to get any easier, with the Nebraska Cornhuskers coming to town, and starting quarterback Dante Moore once again ruled out after the concussion he suffered in Week 4 against the USC Trojans . That will leave either Brock Thomas, Dylan Raiola, or Akili Smith Jr. under center with the start, and a big onus on the offense to show some improvement. While the Big Ten Availability report was released on Wednesday and will again come out on Thursday and Friday nights, we've got some intel on where things stand with each injured player and whether or not they will be able to contribute this weekend. Here's our early look at who we think could potentially be out or limited in this game on Friday night. There was some hope that Dante Moore might be able to give it a go this week after returning to practice following his concussion, but the fact that he was ruled "out" in the first availability report, and not even "questionable," is not a great sign for an expedient return. We will see if Moore is able to go next week against Illinois, but it could still be a couple of weeks before we see No. 5 back on the field, if at all. McClellan has been out for a few weeks now after suffering a broken foot in warmups before the Portland State game, and has been seen wearing a walking boot during games. We will see when he is able to get out of the boot and back to practice, but it might still be several weeks, at the least. "He's going to be done for the foreseeable future. (It's) something he tried to tough out. You know, credit to him. Sometimes you can play through that, but you're probably not going to play as well. But it's one of those ones where it made sense to get it repaired for him." According to head coach Dan Lanning, Platt is still dealing with an undisclosed injury that held him out of the spring game earlier this year. Oregon's coach does not expect him to return to the field anytime soon. "He's gonna be limited for a while with the injury he felt in the spring," Lanning said of Platt. "I don't want to put a timeline on it, but he's going to be out for some time until we see where he's at and continue to progress and challenge himself." After suffering a neck injury during fall camp a year ago, Gresham was held out for the entire 2025 season and has yet to return to the field. Oregon still has him on the roster, but it doesn't sound like he will be back anytime soon. Colorado transfer RB Simeon Price is yet to play this year and has been seen in street clothes wearing a walking boot recently during Oregon games. home.headline: Dante Moore’s Status Isn’t Oregon’s Only Concern on Latest Injury Report
home.blurb: While Wednesday’s injury report provided an initial update on where quarterback Dante Moore stands in his return from a concussion sustained on Sept. 26 against USC, the Ducks’ quarterback woes are more complex than that. In addition to Moore’s availability, Wednesday also offered clarity – and concern – on Oregon’s defensive back situation. Lanning told reporters ahead of the release that starting safety Aaron Flowers will be out for “the foreseeable future,” indicating the Ducks have another starting position to fill.
